products.name: Dialysis Bloodline Sets (Arterial & Venous)
products.description: Dialysis bloodline sets are sterile, single-use tubing circuits that connect a patient's vascular access to a hemodialysis machine, carrying blood from the patient through the dialyzer and back. Each set comprises an arterial line, venous line, drip chambers and connectors matched to a specific dialysis machine brand/model, and is central to safe, leak-free extracorporeal circulation during treatment. Bloodline sets must be compatible with the dialysis machine in use and are typically supplied by the machine manufacturer or an approved third-party vendor.
products.specifications: Sterile, single-patient-use PVC (often DEHP-free) tubing; arterial and venous drip chambers; luer-lock and machine-specific connectors; adult and pediatric set sizes; compatibility varies by dialysis machine brand (e.g., Fresenius, Nipro, B. Braun) — always match set to the specific machine model.
products.sizes: Adult and pediatric sets; standard and low-volume/high-flux circuit variants
products.precautions: Single patient use only — do not reuse or reprocess; must be compatible with the specific dialysis machine model; inspect for leaks/air prior to use; incorrect priming can cause air embolism or blood loss.
products.useSetting: Hemodialysis units, hospital renal wards, dialysis centers

products.name: Hemodialysis Dialyzers
products.description: Hemodialysis dialyzers (artificial kidneys) are sterile, single-use filter cartridges containing thousands of semi-permeable hollow fibers that remove waste products, excess fluid and electrolytes from a patient's blood during dialysis. Dialyzers vary by membrane material, surface area and flux (low-flux vs high-flux), which determine clearance performance and are selected according to the patient's clinical needs and treatment prescription.
products.specifications: Hollow-fiber membrane (polysulfone, polyethersulfone, cellulose-based, etc.); surface area typically 1.0–2.2 m²; low-flux and high-flux variants; sterilized by steam, gamma or ETO; single-use, though some facilities reprocess under strict protocols where permitted.
products.reuse: Disposable (single-use; reprocessing only under strict facility protocol where permitted)
products.sizes: Surface area 1.0–2.2 m²; low-flux and high-flux models
products.precautions: Select membrane/flux according to physician prescription; first-use syndrome/allergic reaction possible with certain membranes; do not reuse unless facility has a validated, regulator-compliant reprocessing protocol.
products.useSetting: Hemodialysis units, dialysis centers, hospital renal wards

products.name: Surgical Sutures (Absorbable & Non-Absorbable)
products.description: Surgical sutures are sterile threads used to close wounds, incisions and surgical sites by approximating tissue edges to support healing. They are available in absorbable forms (which break down naturally in the body) and non-absorbable forms (which require removal or remain permanently), in a wide range of materials, thicknesses and needle configurations to suit different tissue types and procedures.
products.specifications: Absorbable (e.g., polyglactin, catgut, poliglecaprone) and non-absorbable (e.g., nylon, silk, polypropylene) materials; USP sizes typically 10-0 to 2; supplied pre-loaded on needles of varying curvature/type (cutting, reverse-cutting, tapered); sterile, individually packaged.
products.precautions: Select material/size according to tissue type and procedure; needlestick injury risk during handling; verify expiry date and sterile packaging integrity before use.
products.useSetting: Operating theatre, minor surgery/procedure rooms, emergency department

products.name: AV Fistula Needles
products.description: Arteriovenous (AV) fistula needles are sterile, single-use needles designed to cannulate a patient's fistula or graft to establish blood flow access for hemodialysis. They come in arterial and venous configurations, often with back-eye designs and safety mechanisms to reduce accidental needlestick injury to staff.
products.specifications: Stainless steel needle with wing/butterfly grip; gauge typically 15G–17G; back-eye or standard tip; fixed or detachable tubing with clamp; safety (needle-guard) and non-safety variants; sterile, single-use.
products.precautions: Needlestick injury risk — safety-engineered devices recommended; correct cannulation technique required to avoid infiltration/hematoma; single use only.

products.name: Dialysis Concentrate / Bicarbonate Cartridges
products.description: Dialysis concentrates and bicarbonate cartridges supply the acid and bicarbonate components that the dialysis machine mixes with purified water to form dialysate, the fluid that draws waste products and excess fluid from the patient's blood across the dialyzer membrane. Bicarbonate is commonly supplied as a dry cartridge that the machine reconstitutes on-line, while acid concentrate is typically liquid.
products.specifications: Liquid acid concentrate (drums/jugs) and dry bicarbonate cartridges; formulation must match dialysis machine brand/model and prescribed electrolyte profile; shelf-stable when unopened, limited use-life once connected.
products.sterility: Non-sterile (pharmaceutical-grade solution, not for direct injection)
products.sizes: Bicarbonate cartridges ~650–900 g; acid concentrate containers 5–10 L, machine-dependent
products.precautions: Must match the specific dialysis machine and prescribed formulation; incorrect electrolyte concentration can cause serious patient harm; store per manufacturer instructions and check expiry before connecting.

products.name: Closed-System Transfer Devices (CSTD)
products.description: Closed-system transfer devices are mechanical drug-transfer devices used mainly with hazardous drugs such as chemotherapy agents, preventing the transfer of environmental contaminants into the system and the escape of hazardous drug or vapour out of the system during reconstitution, transfer and administration. They protect pharmacy and nursing staff from occupational exposure to cytotoxic medications.
products.specifications: Needle-free, air-tight/closed mechanical connection; compatible vial adaptors, syringe adaptors and spike/bag connectors; typically single-use; brand-specific compatibility across components (adaptors must match the connector system).
products.sizes: Vial adaptor, syringe adaptor, bag/line connector components sold as a compatible set
products.precautions: Components from different CSTD brands are generally not interchangeable; staff require training on correct connection technique; intended to reduce, not eliminate, hazardous drug exposure risk — follow full PPE protocols.
products.useSetting: Oncology/chemotherapy units, hospital pharmacy compounding areas

products.name: Needleless IV Connectors
products.description: Needleless connectors are small valved devices attached to IV catheters, central lines or administration sets that allow clinicians to access the vascular system with a syringe or tubing without using a needle, reducing needlestick injury risk while maintaining a closed system to limit contamination and air embolism.
products.specifications: Luer-activated or split-septum valve mechanisms; positive-, negative- or neutral-displacement designs; compatible with standard luer-lock syringes/tubing; sterile, single-use, typically changed every 72–96 hours or per facility protocol.
products.sizes: Standard luer-lock fitting; single-use, low priming volume
products.precautions: Disinfect connector surface ("scrub the hub") before each access to prevent catheter-related bloodstream infection; replace per facility protocol/manufacturer instructions; do not reuse.
products.useSetting: Wards, ICU, dialysis units, oncology units, home infusion
products.endUser: Nurses, dialysis technicians, infusion therapy staff

products.name: Surgical Staplers (Skin & Internal)
products.description: Surgical staplers are devices used to close skin incisions or internal tissue (such as bowel, vascular or lung tissue) quickly and with consistent tension, using titanium or stainless-steel staples instead of sutures. Skin staplers are typically simple disposable devices for wound closure, while internal/linear and circular staplers are more complex devices used during open or laparoscopic surgery to cut and staple tissue simultaneously.
products.specifications: Disposable skin staplers (25–35 regular staples per device) and linear/circular internal staplers with reloadable cartridges; staple leg length and row configuration vary by tissue type; single-use devices, some internal stapler handles are reusable with disposable cartridges.
products.reuse: Disposable (skin staplers; internal cartridges); some internal stapler handles reusable
products.sizes: Skin staplers ~25–35 staples; internal cartridges in multiple staple-height/length options
products.precautions: Select cartridge/staple height according to tissue thickness; internal stapling requires surgical training; check for staple line bleeding/leak before closing.

products.name: Hemostatic Products & Devices
products.description: Hemostatic products are topical agents and devices applied to bleeding tissue during surgery or wound care to control hemorrhage when conventional methods (pressure, sutures, cautery) are insufficient or impractical. They include absorbable gelatin/collagen sponges, oxidized cellulose, topical thrombin and hemostatic gauze/powder.
products.specifications: Absorbable collagen/gelatin sponges, oxidized regenerated cellulose, hemostatic gauze impregnated with agents (e.g., kaolin, chitosan), topical thrombin; sterile, single-use; absorbable formats typically resorb over days to weeks.
products.sizes: Various sponge/gauze sizes and pack configurations
products.regulatoryClass: Class II–III depending on formulation (e.g., thrombin-based products are higher risk)
products.precautions: Not a substitute for surgical hemostatic technique in major bleeding; some products derived from animal/human plasma sources carry allergy/transmission-risk warnings; follow product-specific application instructions.

products.name: Leukoreduction Blood Filters
products.description: Leukoreduction filters are sterile, single-use inline filters used during blood collection or transfusion to remove white blood cells (leukocytes) from red cell or platelet products, reducing the risk of febrile transfusion reactions, HLA alloimmunization and transmission of leukocyte-associated viruses such as CMV.
products.specifications: Inline filter housing with polyester/synthetic fibre filter media; pre-storage (at collection) or bedside (pre-transfusion) filter types; compatible with standard blood bag tubing/spikes; sterile, single-use.
products.sizes: Standard unit-volume filters (~250–450 mL blood bag compatible)
products.precautions: Follow correct priming to avoid air introduction; filtration is time-sensitive — follow blood bank/manufacturer protocol; not a substitute for other blood safety screening.
products.useSetting: Blood bank, transfusion service, hospital wards/ICU

products.name: Chemotherapy Administration Sets (Non-DEHP Tubing)
products.description: Chemotherapy administration sets are IV giving sets specifically manufactured with non-DEHP, non-PVC tubing to prevent leaching of plasticizers into cytotoxic drug solutions and to reduce drug absorption into the tubing wall, ensuring accurate cytotoxic drug delivery. They typically include connectors compatible with CSTD systems for staff safety.
products.specifications: Non-DEHP, non-PVC (e.g., polyethylene-lined) tubing; drip chamber, roller clamp, and CSTD-compatible or luer-lock connectors; light-protected tubing available for photosensitive drugs; sterile, single-use.
products.sizes: Standard adult IV set lengths; light-protected and non-light-protected variants
products.precautions: Use only non-DEHP sets for cytotoxic infusions; handle as hazardous drug waste after use; combine with CSTD and full PPE per chemotherapy safe-handling protocol.

products.name: Peripherally Inserted Central Catheters (PICC)
products.description: A peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC) is a long, thin, sterile catheter inserted through a peripheral vein (usually in the upper arm) and advanced until its tip sits in a large central vein near the heart, providing reliable venous access for extended IV therapy, chemotherapy, parenteral nutrition or frequent blood draws over weeks to months.
products.specifications: Polyurethane or silicone catheter; single-, double- or triple-lumen configurations; typically 4–6 Fr for adults; lengths adjustable/trimmable at insertion; may include antimicrobial or power-injectable variants; sterile, single-patient use, inserted under ultrasound guidance.
products.precautions: Requires trained inserter and, ideally, ultrasound/ECG-tip-confirmation guidance; risk of catheter-related bloodstream infection, thrombosis or malposition; strict aseptic insertion and dressing-care protocol required.
products.useSetting: Hospital wards, oncology units, home infusion therapy

products.name: Surgical Meshes (Hernia Repair)
products.description: Surgical meshes are sterile, flexible implants used to reinforce or bridge weakened tissue, most commonly in hernia repair, providing structural support while the body's own tissue grows into or around the mesh. Meshes are available in synthetic non-absorbable, partially absorbable and biologic materials, selected according to the repair site and patient risk factors.
products.specifications: Synthetic (polypropylene, polyester), absorbable/partially-absorbable and biologic (animal-derived collagen) mesh materials; flat sheet or pre-shaped/plug formats; various pore sizes and weights (lightweight to heavyweight); sterile, single-use implant.
products.sizes: Sheet sizes commonly ~6x11 cm to 30x30 cm; pre-shaped plug/patch options
products.regulatoryClass: Class II–III (implantable device; class depends on material/indication)
products.precautions: Material selection affects infection risk, adhesion formation and recurrence rate; contraindicated/cautioned in contaminated fields for some synthetic meshes; verify sterility and expiry before implantation.

products.name: Blood Bags (Collection Sets)
products.description: Blood bags are sterile, single-use plastic collection sets used to collect, separate, store and transfuse whole blood and its components (red cells, plasma, platelets). Sets range from single bags for simple collection to multi-bag (double/triple/quadruple) systems that allow component separation by centrifugation without breaking the closed, sterile system.
products.specifications: PVC (DEHP or DEHP-free) bags with integral anticoagulant (e.g., CPDA-1, CPD) pre-filled in the primary bag; single, double, triple or quadruple bag configurations; integral collection needle and tubing; sterile, single-use, closed system.
products.sizes: Primary bag ~450–500 mL capacity; satellite bags vary by configuration
products.precautions: Maintain closed-system sterility throughout collection/processing; correct anticoagulant-to-blood ratio is critical; store and transport per blood bank temperature requirements.
products.useSetting: Blood bank, mobile blood donation drives, transfusion service

products.name: Central Venous Catheters (CVC)
products.description: Central venous catheters are sterile catheters inserted into a large central vein (internal jugular, subclavian or femoral) to provide vascular access for fluid/medication administration, hemodynamic monitoring, or when peripheral access is inadequate. They are typically inserted at the bedside or in theatre using ultrasound guidance and sterile technique, and may remain in place for days to weeks.
products.specifications: Polyurethane catheter, single- to quadruple-lumen; typical adult sizes 7–8.5 Fr; antimicrobial/antithrombogenic-coated variants available; insertion kit usually includes guidewire, dilator, introducer needle and fixation device; sterile, single-patient use.
products.sizes: 7–8.5 Fr (adult), 4–7 Fr (pediatric); single to quadruple lumen
products.precautions: Risk of catheter-related bloodstream infection, pneumothorax (subclavian/jugular) and thrombosis; requires trained inserter, maximal sterile barrier precautions and radiographic tip confirmation.

products.name: Antimicrobial Wound Dressings (Silver / PHMB)
products.description: Antimicrobial dressings incorporate agents such as silver (Ag) or polyhexamethylene biguanide (PHMB) into the dressing material to reduce bacterial bioburden at the wound surface, helping manage infected or high-risk chronic and post-surgical wounds alongside standard wound-care protocols.
products.specifications: Silver-impregnated foam, hydrofiber, alginate or gauze formats; PHMB-impregnated gauze/foam; absorbent or non-absorbent backing; sizes typically 5x5 cm to 15x15 cm or roll format; sterile, single-use.
products.sizes: 5x5 cm to 15x15 cm pads; rolls for larger/irregular wounds
products.precautions: Not a substitute for systemic antibiotics in clinically infected wounds; silver sensitivity is possible; follow manufacturer wear-time recommendations.
products.useSetting: Wards, wound care clinics, home care

products.name: Laparoscopic Disposables / Trocar Sets
products.description: Laparoscopic disposable sets, including trocars, provide sterile single-use access ports and instrumentation for minimally invasive (keyhole) surgery, allowing insertion of the laparoscope and surgical instruments through small abdominal incisions while maintaining pneumoperitoneum.
products.specifications: Bladed or bladeless trocar tips; cannula diameters typically 5 mm, 10 mm and 12 mm; insufflation valve and seal mechanisms; may include disposable Veress needles, specimen retrieval bags and other single-use laparoscopic accessories; sterile, single-use.
products.precautions: Risk of visceral/vascular injury on insertion — requires trained surgical technique; verify correct trocar size for the intended instrument; single-use only, do not reprocess.

products.name: Hemodialysis Catheters (Tunneled & Non-Tunneled)
products.description: Hemodialysis catheters are large-bore, dual-lumen central venous catheters designed specifically for hemodialysis, providing immediate vascular access when a fistula or graft is not yet available or usable. Non-tunneled catheters are for short-term/acute use, while tunneled cuffed catheters are designed for longer-term use with a subcutaneous tunnel and cuff that reduces infection risk and aids fixation.
products.specifications: Dual-lumen, large-bore polyurethane catheter; typical size 11.5–14.5 Fr; non-tunneled (acute, days) and tunneled cuffed (chronic, weeks–months) variants; insertion via internal jugular, subclavian or femoral vein under ultrasound guidance; sterile, single-patient use.
products.precautions: High infection and thrombosis risk relative to fistula/graft access — for temporary or bridging use where possible; requires trained inserter and strict aseptic catheter-care protocol; heparin/citrate locking per facility protocol between sessions.
products.useSetting: Hemodialysis units, ICU, hospital renal wards

products.name: IV Cannulas / IV Catheters
products.description: Intravenous (IV) cannulas are short, sterile peripheral catheters inserted into a vein to provide access for fluid, medication or blood product administration and for blood sampling. They are among the most frequently used vascular access devices across nearly all clinical settings. Note: a partner supplier has already been secured for this item, so further supplier sourcing is not required.
products.specifications: Color-coded by gauge (e.g., 14G–24G); winged or non-winged hub; integrated injection port on some models; safety (needle-shielding) and non-safety variants; sterile, single-use.
products.precautions: Needlestick injury risk — safety-engineered devices recommended; site rotation/monitoring needed to reduce phlebitis/infiltration; single use only.

products.name: Foley Catheters (Indwelling Urinary Catheters)
products.description: Foley catheters are sterile, flexible indwelling urinary catheters inserted through the urethra into the bladder to provide continuous urinary drainage. An inflatable balloon near the tip holds the catheter in place once inserted; commonly used for patients needing accurate urine output monitoring, urinary retention management, or peri-operative bladder decompression — including dialysis patients requiring close fluid balance monitoring. Note: Foley catheters also appear under the Urology category elsewhere in this catalog — kept here as well since the item was requested for this list.
products.specifications: Latex or silicone construction; 2-way (drainage only) or 3-way (drainage + irrigation) configurations; balloon capacity typically 5–30 mL; sizes 8–24 Fr; sterile, single-patient use.
products.precautions: Catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI) risk increases with duration of use — remove as soon as clinically appropriate; latex allergy risk with latex catheters — silicone alternative available; maintain closed drainage system.
products.useSetting: Wards, ICU, operating theatre, long-term/home care

products.name: Nitrile Examination Gloves
products.description: Nitrile examination gloves are disposable, latex-free protective gloves used by healthcare professionals during routine patient examinations, specimen handling, cleaning and other tasks where a barrier between the hands and potentially contaminated materials is required. Nitrile provides good resistance to many common chemicals and punctures compared with many thin latex alternatives, while maintaining tactile sensitivity for clinical work. Gloves should be selected according to the intended task, exposure risk and applicable regulatory requirements.
products.specifications: Material: nitrile; powder-free options commonly preferred for clinical environments; sizes typically XS–XL; ambidextrous design common; beaded cuff common; single-use; sterile or non-sterile depending on product; thickness, AQL, tensile strength, chemical resistance and certification must be verified against the specific manufacturer model.
products.precautions: Not for surgical/sterile procedures; check for latex-free labelling if latex-sensitive patients/staff

products.name: Latex Examination Gloves
products.description: Latex examination gloves are disposable protective gloves designed for routine medical examinations, patient care and clinical handling tasks. Natural rubber latex provides elasticity, fit and tactile sensitivity, making it suitable for many general healthcare applications. Because latex proteins can cause allergic reactions in susceptible individuals, facilities should use appropriate risk controls and provide latex-free alternatives where required.
products.specifications: Natural rubber latex; powder-free or powdered versions; sizes commonly XS–XL; ambidextrous; beaded cuff; single-use; sterile/non-sterile options; thickness, tensile strength, AQL and regulatory conformity are manufacturer-specific.
products.precautions: Latex allergy risk to staff and patients – have non-latex alternative available

products.name: Vinyl Examination Gloves
products.description: Vinyl examination gloves are disposable gloves made from synthetic polyvinyl chloride and are generally used for short-duration, low-risk clinical and non-sterile handling activities. They are easy to don and economical for high-volume use, but their fit and barrier performance can differ from nitrile or latex gloves, so they should be selected according to the task and exposure risk.
products.specifications: PVC/vinyl construction; powder-free options; sizes commonly S–XL; ambidextrous; single-use; non-sterile commonly; thickness, cuff length, tensile strength and applicable standards vary by manufacturer.
products.precautions: Lower puncture resistance and fit than nitrile/latex – use only for low-risk, short tasks

products.name: Powder-Free Examination Gloves
products.description: Powder-free examination gloves are disposable medical gloves manufactured without added powder on the inner surface. They are intended to reduce powder-related contamination and irritation while providing a protective barrier for routine patient examination and clinical handling. Material may be nitrile, latex or another approved elastomer, so the material should be specified when purchasing.
products.specifications: Powder-free; material varies; sizes typically XS–XL; ambidextrous; single-use; sterile/non-sterile options; thickness, AQL, tensile strength and barrier performance are model-specific.
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Powdered Examination Gloves
products.description: Powdered examination gloves are non-sterile, single-use gloves lightly dusted on the inside with an absorbable cornstarch powder so they slide on easily and stay comfortable when hands are damp. They are used for routine patient examinations, specimen handling and general nursing care in wards, outpatient clinics and laboratories, and are most often made from natural rubber latex or vinyl in sizes S to XL. Because the powder can carry latex proteins into the air and leave residue on wounds or lab samples, many facilities reserve them for low-risk tasks and choose powder-free gloves for wound care or latex-sensitive staff.
products.specifications: Material may include nitrile, latex, vinyl or polyethylene; sterile/non-sterile; powdered/powder-free; sizes typically XS–XL depending on product; thickness, cuff length, AQL, tensile strength and regulatory conformity are model-specific.
products.precautions: Cornstarch powder may cause tissue reaction if used in sterile fields; increasingly restricted/banned in many jurisdictions

products.name: Disposable PE Gloves
products.description: Disposable PE gloves are thin, loose-fitting gloves cut and heat-sealed from polyethylene film. They give a basic barrier for brief, low-risk tasks such as handling food trays, changing linen, dispensing supplies, applying creams or touching clean surfaces in wards and home care. Because the film is not elastic and the seams are welded rather than moulded, they do not fit closely and puncture easily, so they are not a substitute for examination gloves when contact with blood, body fluids or sharp instruments is expected. They are typically sold in one size or S to L, often in bulk packs or tear-off pads.
products.specifications: Material may include nitrile, latex, vinyl or polyethylene; sterile/non-sterile; powdered/powder-free; sizes typically XS–XL depending on product; thickness, cuff length, AQL, tensile strength and regulatory conformity are model-specific.
products.precautions: Very low barrier protection – food handling/light duty only, not for clinical exposure risk

products.name: Latex Surgical Gloves
products.description: Latex surgical gloves are sterile, single-use gloves made from natural rubber latex and shaped to the hand, with curved fingers and a long cuff that sits over the gown sleeve. Latex offers high elasticity, a close fit and fine tactile sensitivity, which is why it remains common for procedures that need precise instrument handling. They are sized in half sizes from 5.5 to 8.5 and supplied as individually packed pairs. Natural rubber proteins can trigger allergic reactions, so check for latex allergy in both the surgical team and the patient before use, and keep a latex-free alternative available.
products.specifications: Material may include nitrile, latex, vinyl or polyethylene; sterile/non-sterile; powdered/powder-free; sizes typically XS–XL depending on product; thickness, cuff length, AQL, tensile strength and regulatory conformity are model-specific.
products.precautions: Latex allergy risk – confirm patient/staff sensitivity

products.name: Nitrile Surgical Gloves
products.description: Nitrile surgical gloves are sterile, single-use gloves made from synthetic nitrile rubber and are a common latex-free choice for operating theatres and procedure rooms. Nitrile contains no natural rubber proteins, so it suits staff and patients with latex allergy, and it generally offers good puncture and chemical resistance. The gloves are anatomically shaped, sized 5.5 to 8.5 in half sizes and packed as sterile pairs. Nitrile is usually somewhat less elastic than latex, so trying adjacent sizes or a softer formulation helps surgeons find a snug fit without hand fatigue during long cases.
products.specifications: Material may include nitrile, latex, vinyl or polyethylene; sterile/non-sterile; powdered/powder-free; sizes typically XS–XL depending on product; thickness, cuff length, AQL, tensile strength and regulatory conformity are model-specific.
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Powder-Free Surgical Gloves
products.description: Powder-free surgical gloves are sterile, single-use gloves made without donning powder, typically treated by chlorination or given an inner polymer coating that helps the glove slide on. Removing powder reduces the risk of powder-related wound inflammation and adhesions, lowers airborne latex proteins and avoids residue on implants and instruments. They are made in latex and in synthetic materials such as nitrile, polyisoprene or neoprene, in half sizes 5.5 to 8.5. When choosing, look at the base material as well as the coating, since together they determine allergy risk, grip and how easily the glove dons with damp hands.
products.specifications: Material may include nitrile, latex, vinyl or polyethylene; sterile/non-sterile; powdered/powder-free; sizes typically XS–XL depending on product; thickness, cuff length, AQL, tensile strength and regulatory conformity are model-specific.
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Sterile Surgical Gloves
products.description: Sterile surgical gloves are single-use, individually packaged pairs for aseptic procedures where the glove will touch sterile instruments, open wounds or body cavities. Unlike examination gloves, they are sized by hand circumference in half sizes, here 5.5 to 8.5, and are anatomically shaped with long cuffs that overlap the gown sleeve. Beyond the operating theatre, they are used for bedside sterile tasks such as urinary catheter insertion, central line placement and wound procedures. The inner wrapper is folded so gloves can be put on without touching their outer surface; check that the pack is intact and in date before opening.
products.specifications: Material may include nitrile, latex, vinyl or polyethylene; sterile/non-sterile; powdered/powder-free; sizes typically XS–XL depending on product; thickness, cuff length, AQL, tensile strength and regulatory conformity are model-specific.
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Orthopedic Surgical Gloves
products.description: Orthopedic surgical gloves are sterile, single-use surgical gloves made in a heavier gauge than standard surgical gloves to withstand the demands of bone and joint surgery. The thicker wall gives more resistance to tears and punctures from bone fragments, wires, saws and sharp-edged implants, and many have a textured surface for a firm grip on wet instruments. They are commonly sized 6.5 to 9.0. The added thickness reduces tactile sensitivity, so some surgical teams pair them with a thinner inner glove in a double-gloving system rather than relying on gauge alone.
products.specifications: Material may include nitrile, latex, vinyl or polyethylene; sterile/non-sterile; powdered/powder-free; sizes typically XS–XL depending on product; thickness, cuff length, AQL, tensile strength and regulatory conformity are model-specific.
products.precautions: Thicker gauge for cement/bone-fragment protection; may reduce tactile sensitivity

products.name: Chemotherapy Gloves
products.description: Chemotherapy gloves are disposable gloves tested for resistance to permeation by cytotoxic and other hazardous drugs, giving staff a barrier when preparing, administering or disposing of chemotherapy agents and handling contaminated waste or patient excreta. They are usually nitrile or another synthetic rubber, thicker than standard exam gloves, with extended cuffs that can be pulled over a gown sleeve. Non-sterile versions suit drug administration and spill clean-up, while sterile variants are used inside pharmacy compounding cabinets. Double gloving, and changing gloves at set intervals or after any tear or contamination, is standard practice when handling hazardous drugs.
products.specifications: Material may include nitrile, latex, vinyl or polyethylene; sterile/non-sterile; powdered/powder-free; sizes typically XS–XL depending on product; thickness, cuff length, AQL, tensile strength and regulatory conformity are model-specific.
products.precautions: Must be ASTM D6978-tested for chemo drug permeation; double-gloving recommended when handling cytotoxic agents

products.name: Radiation Protection Gloves
products.description: Radiation protection gloves are reusable gloves containing lead or lead-free attenuating materials such as tungsten, bismuth or antimony compounds, designed to reduce scattered radiation dose to the hands during fluoroscopy, interventional radiology, cardiac catheterization and orthopaedic imaging. These non-sterile gloves come in S to XL, from heavier gauntlet styles to thinner, more flexible types for tasks needing dexterity. They are intended for scattered radiation, so hands should still be kept out of the primary beam. Regular visual inspection for cracks and storage flat rather than folded help preserve the protective layer.
products.specifications: Material may include nitrile, latex, vinyl or polyethylene; sterile/non-sterile; powdered/powder-free; sizes typically XS–XL depending on product; thickness, cuff length, AQL, tensile strength and regulatory conformity are model-specific.
products.precautions: Attenuates scatter radiation only – not a substitute for shielding/distance/time precautions

products.name: Thermal/Heat Resistant Gloves
products.description: Thermal or heat-resistant gloves are reusable insulating gloves for safely handling hot items, such as loads removed from autoclaves and dry heat sterilizers, glassware from laboratory ovens, and equipment from hotplates or water baths. They are typically made from aramid or similar heat-resistant fibres, silicone-coated fabric or insulated cotton, often with a long gauntlet cuff to protect the wrist and forearm, in sizes S to XL. Check the rated contact temperature against the task, and note that fabric gloves insulate poorly once wet, so steam-heavy work may call for a silicone or water-resistant outer surface.
products.specifications: Material may include nitrile, latex, vinyl or polyethylene; sterile/non-sterile; powdered/powder-free; sizes typically XS–XL depending on product; thickness, cuff length, AQL, tensile strength and regulatory conformity are model-specific.
products.precautions: Inspect for wear before use near autoclaves/heat sources; not a sterile barrier

products.name: Cut-Resistant Medical Gloves
products.description: Cut-resistant medical gloves are reusable knitted gloves made from high-performance fibres such as high-molecular-weight polyethylene, aramid or steel-reinforced yarns that resist slicing from blades and sharp edges. In hospitals and laboratories they are used during manual instrument cleaning and reprocessing, autopsy and pathology work, tissue grossing and handling broken glassware. They are non-sterile and come in S to XL. They resist cuts but give limited protection against needle punctures and none against fluids, so they are usually combined with a disposable glove, and should be laundered or decontaminated according to the manufacturer's instructions.
products.specifications: Material may include nitrile, latex, vinyl or polyethylene; sterile/non-sterile; powdered/powder-free; sizes typically XS–XL depending on product; thickness, cuff length, AQL, tensile strength and regulatory conformity are model-specific.
products.precautions: Reduces but does not eliminate sharps injury/needlestick risk

products.name: Disposable Isolation Gowns
products.description: Disposable isolation gowns are non-sterile, single-use gowns worn over clothing to protect the arms and torso of staff from contact with blood, body fluids and other potentially infectious material during patient care. They are used in isolation rooms, emergency departments and general wards, and are made from polypropylene nonwoven, SMS or film-laminated fabrics with elastic or knitted cuffs and neck and waist ties. They come in universal or free size and XL. Choose the fabric for the expected exposure: lightweight nonwoven for dry contact precautions, and fluid-resistant laminated or coated gowns when splashes are likely.
products.specifications: Material: PP nonwoven, SMS or PE-coated/laminated; Fabric weight: approx. 20–50 gsm; Cuffs: elastic or knitted; Closure: neck and waist ties, open back; Length: below knee; Sterility: non-sterile, single-use
products.precautions: Select fluid-resistance level (AAMI 1–4) to match exposure risk
products.useSetting: All clinical areas; isolation rooms; OR

products.name: Surgical Gowns
products.description: Surgical gowns are sterile gowns worn by the scrub team to maintain the sterile field and act as a barrier against blood and fluid strike-through during operations. The front and sleeves are the critical zones, so many designs add reinforced, fluid-impervious panels there, with knitted cuffs that sit under the glove cuff and a wrap-around back closed with a tie card. Most are single-use SMS or spunlace nonwovens, though reusable woven fabric variants exist. Sizes run S to XL; choose reinforcement and fluid resistance according to the expected length of the procedure and volume of fluid.
products.specifications: Material: SMS, spunlace or laminated nonwoven; Reinforcement: standard or reinforced front and sleeves; Cuffs: knitted; Closure: wrap-around back with neck fastening and tie card; Sterility: sterile, individually packed
products.precautions: Select reinforced/critical-zone gowns for high fluid-exposure procedures
products.useSetting: All clinical areas; isolation rooms; OR

products.name: Patient Gowns
products.description: Patient gowns are loose-fitting garments worn by patients during admission, examinations, imaging and procedures, giving staff easy access to the body while preserving modesty. Traditional designs open at the back and fasten with ties or snaps, and some add shoulder snaps or side openings for IV lines and monitoring leads. Reusable versions are usually cotton or polyester-cotton fabric that withstands repeated laundering, while disposable nonwoven variants suit isolation or short outpatient stays. Sizes include S to XL plus adult and paediatric cuts; a generous back overlap improves coverage and patient comfort.
products.specifications: Material: cotton or poly-cotton (reusable), PP/SMS nonwoven (disposable); Closure: back ties or snaps; Sleeves: short or sleeveless, shoulder snaps on some; Length: approx. knee length; Sterility: non-sterile
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: All clinical areas; isolation rooms; OR

products.name: Coveralls
products.description: Coveralls are one-piece protective suits covering the torso, arms and legs, often with an attached hood, worn when more coverage than a gown is needed, such as caring for patients with highly infectious diseases, handling hazardous spills or decontamination work. They are made from microporous film-laminated nonwoven, SMS or similar fabrics, with elasticated hood, wrists and ankles and a front zip under a storm flap. These are disposable and come in S to XXL. Choose a size with room for bending and reaching, and plan a supervised removal sequence, since taking off a coverall without self-contamination takes practice.
products.specifications: Material: microporous film-laminated PP or SMS nonwoven; Hood: attached, elasticated; Closure: front zip with storm flap; Cuffs/ankles: elasticated; Seams: stitched, bound or taped; Sterility: non-sterile, single-use
products.precautions: Full-body coverage for high-risk isolation/outbreak response; heat stress risk with prolonged wear
products.useSetting: All clinical areas; isolation rooms; OR

products.name: Protective Aprons
products.description: Protective aprons are sleeveless coverings worn over uniforms to protect the front of the body from splashes, spills and soiling during tasks such as bathing patients, emptying drainage bags, handling soiled linen or cleaning instruments. Disposable aprons are thin polyethylene sheets, often supplied on rolls or in flat packs with a neck loop and waist ties, while reusable PVC or rubberized aprons are heavier and suit sluice rooms, CSSD and mortuary work. They are generally one size. Aprons leave the arms and back exposed, so a gown is preferred when arm contact or heavy contamination is expected.
products.specifications: Material: PE film (disposable) or PVC/rubberized fabric (reusable); Width: approx. 70–80 cm; Length: approx. 105–125 cm; Fastening: neck loop and waist ties; Sterility: non-sterile
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: All clinical areas; isolation rooms; OR

products.name: Surgical Masks
products.description: Surgical masks are loose-fitting, disposable face masks worn to protect patients and the sterile field from the wearer's respiratory droplets and to shield the wearer's nose and mouth from splashes. They usually have three layers: a fluid-resistant outer nonwoven, a melt-blown filter layer and a soft inner layer, with a bendable nose wire and either ear loops or tie-on straps. Tie-on styles are common in operating rooms, ear-loop styles on wards and in clinics, and paediatric sizes are available alongside the adult one-size. Because they do not seal to the face, they are not a substitute for a fitted respirator against airborne particles.
products.specifications: Construction, filtration performance, fluid resistance, fit, certification, size and strap configuration vary; respirator fit requirements depend on the specific product and applicable standard.
products.precautions: Fluid-resistant, not an N95-equivalent respirator – does not seal to the face
products.useSetting: All clinical areas; isolation rooms; OR

products.name: N95 Respirators
products.description: N95 respirators are tight-fitting, disposable filtering facepiece respirators designed to filter at least 95 percent of airborne particles, protecting the wearer against aerosols such as those carrying tuberculosis or measles. They come in cup, flat-fold and duckbill shapes with head straps and a malleable nose clip, and some include an exhalation valve. Protection depends on an airtight seal, so users should be fit-tested to a specific model and size, here S, M or L, and perform a seal check every time they put one on. Surgical versions add fluid resistance for use during procedures.
products.specifications: Construction, filtration performance, fluid resistance, fit, certification, size and strap configuration vary; respirator fit requirements depend on the specific product and applicable standard.
products.precautions: Requires fit-testing/fit-check each use; single-use unless manufacturer states extended use is validated
products.useSetting: All clinical areas; isolation rooms; OR

products.name: KN95 Respirators
products.description: KN95 respirators are disposable filtering facepiece respirators made to a performance class requiring at least 95 percent filtration of airborne particles, comparable in filtration to N95 respirators. Most use a folding, multi-layer design with ear loops and a nose clip in a single adult size, which makes them convenient but generally less consistent at achieving a tight face seal than head-strap respirators. They are used for general respiratory protection in clinics, wards and support areas. Where a fit-tested respirator is required, such as during aerosol-generating procedures, confirm the model can pass a fit test before relying on it.
products.specifications: Construction, filtration performance, fluid resistance, fit, certification, size and strap configuration vary; respirator fit requirements depend on the specific product and applicable standard.
products.precautions: Verify certification (GB2626) as equivalency varies by manufacturer; fit-check before use
products.useSetting: All clinical areas; isolation rooms; OR

products.name: Face Shields
products.description: Face shields are clear visors that cover the eyes, nose, mouth and sides of the face, protecting healthcare workers from splashes and sprays of blood, body fluids and chemicals. They consist of a transparent PET, polycarbonate or acetate visor held by a foam headband and elastic strap, or by a reusable frame or glasses-style holder that takes replaceable visors. They can be worn over surgical masks, respirators and prescription glasses. Anti-fog coating and a visor that extends below the chin matter most for comfort and coverage; a face shield does not replace respiratory protection.
products.specifications: Visor material: PET, polycarbonate or acetate; Visor thickness: approx. 0.2–0.5 mm; Coating: anti-fog; Headgear: foam band with elastic strap, or reusable frame; Size: one size, adjustable; Sterility: non-sterile
products.precautions: Used with, not instead of, a mask/respirator
products.useSetting: All clinical areas; isolation rooms; OR

products.name: Bouffant Caps
products.description: Bouffant caps are loose, gathered disposable head covers with an elastic edge, designed to contain all of the hair, including long or thick hair, so that hair and skin flakes do not shed into clean areas. Made from lightweight, breathable polypropylene nonwoven, they are worn in operating rooms, CSSD, pharmacy compounding areas, laboratories and food service. The roomy, pleated shape suits staff with long hair or buns that a fitted surgical cap would not fully cover. They come in one size and should be pulled down to cover the ears and hairline.
products.specifications: Material: spunbond PP nonwoven; Fabric weight: approx. 10–20 gsm; Diameter: approx. 18–24 in (46–61 cm) flat; Edge: elasticated; Sterility: non-sterile, single-use
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: All clinical areas; isolation rooms; OR

products.name: Surgical Caps
products.description: Surgical caps are close-fitting head covers worn by surgeons and theatre staff to keep hair contained and reduce contamination of the surgical field. Common styles include the skull cap, which sits snugly with an elastic band at the back, and the tie-back surgeon's cap, which gives an adjustable, tailored fit; many include an absorbent sweatband across the forehead. Disposable versions are made from spunbond or SMS nonwoven, while reusable cotton caps are also used and must be laundered between uses. Staff with long hair may need a bouffant cap or hood instead, as close-fitting caps can leave hair exposed.
products.specifications: Material: spunbond PP or SMS nonwoven (disposable), cotton or poly-cotton (reusable); Style: skull cap or tie-back surgeon's cap; Fastening: rear ties or elastic; Features: sweatband on some models; Sterility: non-sterile
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: All clinical areas; isolation rooms; OR

products.name: Beard Covers
products.description: Beard covers are disposable nonwoven covers that enclose facial hair on the chin, jaw and lower cheeks, held in place by elastic loops over the ears or around the head. They are worn in operating theatres, sterile compounding areas, CSSD packing rooms, laboratories and hospital kitchens to keep hair from falling onto sterile items, specimens or food. Worn together with a cap or bouffant, they complete head and facial hair coverage. Beard covers do not provide respiratory protection, and wearers who need a respirator should note that facial hair under the seal prevents a proper fit.
products.specifications: Material: spunbond PP nonwoven; Fastening: elastic ear loops or head band; Coverage: chin, jaw and lower cheeks; Size: one size; Sterility: non-sterile, single-use
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: All clinical areas; isolation rooms; OR

products.name: Shoe Covers
products.description: Shoe covers are disposable overshoes that slip over footwear to limit tracking of dirt and contaminants into clean areas and to protect shoes from spills. They are made from polypropylene nonwoven, polyethylene film or CPE with an elasticated ankle opening, and some have a textured anti-skid sole for wet floors. They are used at entrances to operating theatres, ICUs, cleanrooms, laboratories and during home visits. Plain film covers can be slippery on smooth floors, so anti-skid versions are preferable where staff move quickly; for heavy fluid exposure, taller boot covers give better coverage.
products.specifications: Material: PP nonwoven, PE or CPE film; Opening: elasticated ankle; Sole: plain or anti-skid textured; Size: one size, XL for large footwear; Sterility: non-sterile, single-use
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: All clinical areas; isolation rooms; OR

products.name: Boot Covers
products.description: Boot covers are disposable, calf- or knee-length overshoes that cover footwear and the lower leg, giving more protection than standard shoe covers when floors may be wet with blood, irrigation fluid or other contaminated liquids. They are used in operating rooms, delivery suites, autopsy rooms and isolation areas and during spill clean-up, and are often worn with coveralls. Most are polypropylene nonwoven or film-coated fabric with ties or elastic at the top, and many have a non-slip sole. Choose fluid-resistant coated versions for wet procedures and check that the top closure stays up during movement.
products.specifications: Material: PP nonwoven, SMS or PE-coated/laminated; Height: calf to knee length; Top closure: ties or elastic; Sole: non-slip on many models; Size: one size, XL; Sterility: non-sterile, single-use
products.precautions: Higher fluid-resistance than shoe covers; used for high-splash procedures
products.useSetting: All clinical areas; isolation rooms; OR

products.name: Autoclaves
products.description: Autoclaves are pressurized chambers that sterilize reusable instruments, glassware, linen and media with saturated steam, typically at about 121°C or 134°C for a validated exposure time. They range from 10-litre benchtop units for dental and outpatient clinics to 100-litre-plus units for operating theatres, CSSD and laboratories. Gravity-displacement models suit solid, unwrapped items and liquids, while pre-vacuum models actively remove air and are needed for wrapped packs, porous loads and hollow instruments. When choosing, match chamber size and cycle types to your usual loads, and plan for routine indicator testing and the water quality the unit requires.
products.specifications: Sterilization method: saturated steam; common cycle temperatures include approximately 121°C and 134°C, depending on load and validated cycle; chamber capacity varies widely; programmable cycles; pressure/temperature monitoring; safety interlocks; drying and data-recording options vary; electrical supply and water requirements are model-specific.
products.precautions: Requires validated cycle monitoring (chemical + biological indicators); routine maintenance/calibration essential
products.endUser: CSSD technicians, nurses, infection control staff

products.name: Steam Sterilizers
products.description: Steam sterilizers use saturated steam under pressure to kill microorganisms on heat- and moisture-tolerant medical devices and are the main sterilization method in most central sterile services departments. A typical cycle has an air-removal stage, often a series of vacuum pulses, followed by the sterilizing exposure and a drying phase so packs leave the chamber dry. Units range from small benchtop machines for wards and clinics to large floor-standing or pass-through sterilizers fed by the hospital steam supply or an integral generator. Daily air-removal testing, routine load monitoring and adequate water, power and drainage are central to reliable operation.
products.specifications: Sterilization method: saturated steam; common cycle temperatures include approximately 121°C and 134°C, depending on load and validated cycle; chamber capacity varies widely; programmable cycles; pressure/temperature monitoring; safety interlocks; drying and data-recording options vary; electrical supply and water requirements are model-specific.
products.sizes: Small benchtop to large floor-standing units
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.endUser: CSSD technicians, nurses, infection control staff

products.name: Dry Heat Sterilizers
products.description: Dry heat sterilizers sterilize items with hot air rather than steam, typically at around 160–180°C, with longer exposure times needed at the lower temperatures. They suit materials that steam would damage or cannot penetrate, such as laboratory glassware, metal instruments prone to corrosion or dulling, powders, oils and petroleum-based products. Benchtop units with forced-air circulation heat more evenly and run shorter cycles than static gravity-convection ovens. Because the high temperatures can damage plastics, rubber and some instrument coatings, check item compatibility first, and allow loads to cool fully before handling.
products.specifications: Sterilization technology may be steam, low-temperature gas/plasma, dry heat or another validated method; chamber/load capacity, cycle temperature, pressure, time, drying, monitoring and documentation features vary by model.
products.precautions: Longer cycle times than steam; not suitable for heat-sensitive plastics
products.endUser: CSSD technicians, nurses, infection control staff

products.name: Plasma Sterilizers
products.description: Plasma sterilizers are low-temperature sterilizers that use vaporized hydrogen peroxide, energized into a plasma state, to sterilize heat- and moisture-sensitive devices such as endoscopic accessories, cameras, cables, batteries and some plastic instruments. Cycles run at low temperatures, generally below about 55°C, are relatively short, and leave mainly water vapour and oxygen as by-products, so loads need no aeration. Items must be clean and completely dry, and cellulose materials such as paper, linen and gauze cannot be processed, so compatible non-cellulose wraps and pouches are required. Lumen length and diameter limits vary by cycle and should be checked before loading.
products.specifications: Sterilization technology may be steam, low-temperature gas/plasma, dry heat or another validated method; chamber/load capacity, cycle temperature, pressure, time, drying, monitoring and documentation features vary by model.
products.precautions: For heat/moisture-sensitive instruments; hydrogen peroxide plasma cycle requires trained operators
products.endUser: CSSD technicians, nurses, infection control staff

products.name: UV Sterilization Cabinets
products.description: UV sterilization cabinets are enclosed units that expose items to ultraviolet-C light to reduce microbial contamination on the surfaces of objects such as stethoscopes, phones, tablets, keyboards, clean instruments in storage and other small reusable items. They range from small benchtop cabinets to walk-in units, and typically combine UV-C lamps with a cycle timer, door safety interlock and reflective interior. UV acts only where light reaches directly, so shadowed areas, crevices and soiled surfaces are not reliably treated. These cabinets disinfect surfaces and do not replace steam or other validated sterilization of critical devices.
products.specifications: UV source: low-pressure mercury or LED UV-C lamps; Wavelength: approx. 254 nm (mercury), approx. 260–280 nm (LED); Controls: cycle timer, door safety interlock; Interior: stainless steel or reflective lining with shelves or racks; Capacity: benchtop cabinet to walk-in unit
products.precautions: UV is a surface disinfection aid, not a substitute for validated sterilization of critical instruments
products.endUser: CSSD technicians, nurses, infection control staff

products.name: Sterilization Pouches
products.description: Sterilization pouches are self-sealing or heat-sealable packages with a transparent plastic film on one side and medical-grade paper on the other, used to package instruments so they can be sterilized and then kept sterile until use. Steam or gas penetrates through the paper while the film lets staff see the contents, and most carry printed process indicators that change colour after exposure. They come as flat pouches and gusseted or flat rolls, from about 65 x 100 mm up to 300 x 600 mm and rolls cut to length. Avoid overfilling, leave space around the item, and confirm the pouch type suits the sterilization method.
products.specifications: Construction: medical-grade paper with laminated PET/PP film; Sealing: self-seal adhesive strip or heat seal; Formats: flat pouches, flat or gusseted rolls; Indicators: printed process indicators (steam and/or EO); Sizes: approx. 65 x 100 mm to 300 x 600 mm
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.endUser: CSSD technicians, nurses, infection control staff

products.name: Sterilization Wraps
products.description: Sterilization wraps are flat sheets used to enclose instrument trays and linen packs before sterilization, letting the sterilant penetrate while forming a microbial barrier that keeps contents sterile during storage and transport. Disposable wraps are usually SMS polypropylene nonwoven or medical crepe paper, made in different weights for light to heavy trays. They are folded using envelope or square techniques, often in two layers, and secured with indicator tape. Sheets range from about 60 x 60 cm to 100 x 100 cm or larger; choose a size that allows complete coverage with overlapping folds and a weight that resists tearing at tray corners.
products.specifications: Material: SMS polypropylene nonwoven or medical crepe paper; Weight: light to heavy grades, approx. 35–80 gsm; Sizes: approx. 60 x 60 cm to 100 x 100 cm and larger; Compatibility: steam and EO, PP wraps also for hydrogen peroxide plasma; Sterility: non-sterile until processed
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.endUser: CSSD technicians, nurses, infection control staff

products.name: Chemical Indicators
products.description: Chemical indicators are strips, tapes, labels and inserts printed with ink that changes colour or form when exposed to sterilization conditions, giving a quick visual check that a pack or load has been processed. They are grouped into classes, from simple process indicators such as autoclave tape (Class 1) that separate processed from unprocessed items, through Bowie-Dick air-removal test sheets (Class 2), to integrating and emulating indicators (Classes 5 and 6) placed inside packs that respond to time, temperature and sterilant together. A passed indicator supports but does not prove sterility, so results are read alongside physical and biological monitoring.
products.specifications: Formats: indicator tape, strips, labels, Bowie-Dick test sheets; Classes: Class 1 process to Class 6 emulating; Processes: steam, EO, dry heat or hydrogen peroxide (method-specific); Readout: colour change or moving ink bar; Use: single-use, inside and/or outside packs
products.precautions: Confirms exposure to sterilization parameters only – not a substitute for biological indicators
products.endUser: CSSD technicians, nurses, infection control staff

products.name: Biological Indicators
products.description: Biological indicators are test devices containing a known population of highly resistant bacterial spores, used to confirm that a sterilization cycle actually kills microorganisms. After processing in the most challenging location of a load, the indicator is incubated: no growth shows the cycle was lethal, while growth signals a failure to investigate. Self-contained vials holding spores and growth medium together are common, alongside spore strips. Steam and hydrogen peroxide indicators typically use Geobacillus stearothermophilus, while ethylene oxide and dry heat use Bacillus atrophaeus. An unprocessed control from the same lot should be incubated with each test.
products.specifications: Organism: G. stearothermophilus (steam, H2O2) or B. atrophaeus (EO, dry heat); Spore population: typically approx. 10^5–10^6; Format: self-contained vial or spore strip; Incubation: approx. 55–60°C or 35–37°C by organism; Readout: colour change or fluorescence, rapid to 24–48 h
products.precautions: Gold standard for confirming sterilization efficacy; requires incubator and defined read times
products.endUser: CSSD technicians, nurses, infection control staff

products.name: Sterilization Containers
products.description: Sterilization containers are reusable rigid boxes, usually aluminium or high-temperature polymer, that hold instrument sets through sterilization, storage and transport to the operating room. Filters or valves in the lid, and sometimes the base, let steam in and out while maintaining a microbial barrier afterwards, and latching lids with tamper-evident seals show the set has not been opened. They come in half, three-quarter and full sizes to fit standard instrument baskets. Compared with disposable wraps they resist tearing and stack well, but gaskets, latches and filters need regular inspection, and cycles must be validated for rigid containers.
products.specifications: Material: anodized aluminium or high-temperature polymer; Barrier: disposable or long-life filters, or valve system; Sizes: half, three-quarter and full; Closure: latching lid with tamper-evident seal and label holder; Compatibility: steam, some models for low-temperature methods
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.endUser: CSSD technicians, nurses, infection control staff

products.name: Instrument Trays
products.description: Instrument trays are reusable stainless steel trays and baskets used to organise, hold and transport surgical instruments through cleaning, inspection, packing and sterilization. Perforated or wire mesh baskets let water, detergent and steam circulate and drain, while solid trays are used for laying out instruments or as procedure trays. Many sets use silicone mats, pins or brackets to keep delicate instruments separated and protected. They come in small to large sizes, with or without lids and handles. Choose a size that holds the set in a single layer, as overloading hampers cleaning, steam penetration and drying.
products.specifications: Material: stainless steel (304 or 316 grade); Style: perforated, wire mesh or solid, with or without lid; Sizes: small to large, often sized to fit standard containers; Accessories: silicone mats, instrument pins, handles; Compatibility: washer-disinfector and steam sterilization
products.sizes: Various – small to large stainless trays
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.endUser: CSSD technicians, nurses, infection control staff

products.name: Disinfectant Sprayers
products.description: Disinfectant sprayers are reusable devices that apply disinfectant solutions to surfaces, equipment and rooms in an even, controlled spray. Handheld trigger and pump-pressure sprayers of 0.5 to 5 litres suit spot treatment of bed areas, trolleys and benches, while larger battery-powered electrostatic units cover wider areas with charged droplets that wrap around surfaces. Bottles and seals must be chemically compatible with the product used, such as chlorine, alcohol or quaternary ammonium disinfectants. Surfaces must stay wet for the disinfectant's stated contact time, and in many settings spraying onto a cloth is preferred to reduce aerosol exposure.
products.specifications: Type: trigger, pump-pressure or electrostatic; Capacity: 0.5–5 L handheld, larger units available; Nozzle: adjustable mist to jet; Materials: chemical-resistant HDPE/PP with resistant seals; Power: manual or rechargeable battery
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.endUser: CSSD technicians, nurses, infection control staff

products.name: Surface Disinfectants
products.description: Surface disinfectants are liquid solutions and pre-moistened wipes used to clean and disinfect environmental surfaces and non-critical equipment such as bed rails, trolleys, examination couches, countertops and monitors. Common active ingredients include alcohols, quaternary ammonium compounds, chlorine-releasing agents, hydrogen peroxide and blends, which differ in spectrum of activity, contact time and material compatibility. They are supplied in 500 mL to 5 L bottles and wipe tubs. When choosing, check activity against the organisms of concern, the wet contact time required, and compatibility with plastics and screens, as some agents damage materials with repeated use.
products.specifications: Actives: alcohol, QAC, chlorine, hydrogen peroxide or blends; Format: ready-to-use liquid, concentrate or pre-saturated wipes; Pack sizes: 500 mL–5 L bottles, wipe tubs; Contact time: typically approx. 1–10 min, product-specific; Use: non-critical surfaces and equipment
products.precautions: Confirm contact/kill time and compatibility with surface material
products.endUser: CSSD technicians, nurses, infection control staff

products.name: Instrument Disinfectants
products.description: Instrument disinfectants are chemical solutions used to disinfect reusable medical devices that cannot be heat sterilized, or to decontaminate instruments before further processing. High-level disinfectants such as glutaraldehyde, ortho-phthalaldehyde and peracetic acid are used for semi-critical devices like endoscopes and ultrasound probes, while lower-level detergent-disinfectant formulations suit general instruments and pre-soaking. They are supplied as concentrates for dilution or ready-to-use solutions in 1 to 5 litre containers. Instruments must be thoroughly cleaned first, fully immersed for the stated contact time and rinsed afterwards, and reusable solutions need regular concentration testing.
products.specifications: Actives: glutaraldehyde, OPA, peracetic acid, hydrogen peroxide or QAC-based; Level: high-level or intermediate/low-level; Format: concentrate or ready-to-use; Pack sizes: 1–5 L; Reuse: single-use or reusable for a stated period with test strips
products.precautions: High-level disinfection does not replace sterilization for critical instruments
products.endUser: CSSD technicians, nurses, infection control staff

products.name: Hand Sanitizers
products.description: Hand sanitizers are alcohol-based hand rubs used for hand hygiene at the point of care when hands are not visibly soiled, such as before and after patient contact and before aseptic tasks. Most contain ethanol or isopropanol, commonly 60–80 percent, with emollients to limit skin dryness, and come as gels, liquids or foams. Sizes range from 100 mL pocket bottles and pump bottles to 1–5 L refills for wall dispensers. Use enough to cover all hand surfaces and rub until dry, usually 20–30 seconds; soap and water is still needed for visibly soiled hands and some spore-forming organisms.
products.specifications: Active: ethanol or isopropanol, approx. 60–80% v/v; Format: gel, liquid or foam; Additives: emollients; Pack sizes: 100 mL–5 L, pump bottles and refills; Dispensing: flip-top, pump or wall dispenser
products.precautions: Alcohol-based (≥60–70%) products are flammable – store away from ignition sources
products.endUser: CSSD technicians, nurses, infection control staff

products.name: Alcohol Preparations
products.description: Alcohol preparations are isopropyl or ethyl alcohol products, commonly around 70 percent, used for skin antisepsis before injections and venepuncture and for wiping injection ports, vial stoppers and small equipment. Single-use formats include individually sealed prep pads, swabs and sachets, while bulk bottles from 500 mL to 5 L are used for general antisepsis and wiping. Sterile swab variants are available for procedures that require them. Alcohol acts quickly but evaporates fast and leaves no lasting effect, so allow the skin to dry fully before puncture, and keep containers closed and away from flames.
products.specifications: Active: isopropyl or ethyl alcohol, typically 70%; Formats: prep pads, swabs, sachets, bottles; Pad material: nonwoven, single or multi-ply; Pack sizes: single sachets to 500 mL–5 L; Sterility: non-sterile, sterile swab variants available
products.precautions: Flammable; avoid use near active cautery/oxygen sources
products.endUser: CSSD technicians, nurses, infection control staff

products.name: Patient Monitors
products.description: Patient monitors are bedside devices that continuously measure and display vital signs, commonly ECG, heart rate, SpO2, non-invasive blood pressure, temperature and respiration, with waveforms, trends and alarms. They are used in ICUs, wards, operating and recovery rooms and emergency departments, and range from compact transport units to modular monitors that accept extra parameters such as invasive pressures or capnography. Battery backup keeps monitoring going during patient moves. When choosing, consider the parameters needed now and later, screen size, alarm management, adult, paediatric and neonatal settings, and whether the unit can network to a central station.
products.specifications: Parameters: ECG, SpO2, NIBP, temperature, respiration; Options: IBP, EtCO2 on modular models; Display: colour screen, approx. 8–17 in; Patient types: adult, paediatric, neonatal; Power: mains with battery backup; Connectivity: wired or wireless link to central station
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Blood Pressure Monitors
products.description: Blood pressure monitors measure arterial blood pressure non-invasively with an inflatable cuff around the upper arm, either automatically by oscillometric sensing or manually with a gauge and stethoscope. In hospitals they are used for routine vital signs on wards, spot checks in outpatient clinics, triage in emergency departments and scheduled repeat readings in critical care. Options include portable desktop units, units on mobile stands and devices that also record pulse rate and store readings. Accurate results depend heavily on the correct cuff, so keep adult, large adult and paediatric cuffs available and choose by measured arm circumference.
products.specifications: Automated or manual measurement; adult, large-adult, pediatric and neonatal cuff options; pressure measurement range and accuracy vary; memory, averaging, alarms and connectivity vary on electronic models; cuff sizes must match patient arm circumference.
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Pulse Oximeters
products.description: Pulse oximeters estimate arterial oxygen saturation (SpO2) and pulse rate non-invasively by passing red and infrared light through a fingertip, earlobe or foot and measuring how much is absorbed. Fingertip models suit quick spot checks, while handheld and tabletop units with cable probes allow continuous monitoring, alarms and trend storage in wards, ICUs and emergency departments. Reusable clip and wrap probes come in adult, paediatric and neonatal sizes, and disposable covers or sensors reduce cross-contamination. Readings can be affected by poor circulation, movement, nail polish, cold extremities and skin pigmentation, so interpret values alongside the clinical picture.
products.specifications: Parameters: SpO2 and pulse rate; sensor technology: optical; display type varies; adult/pediatric/neonatal sensors may be available; battery operation common; measurement range, accuracy, averaging time, alarm functions and data connectivity are model-specific.
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Digital Thermometers
products.description: Digital thermometers are electronic contact thermometers that use a sensor in the probe tip to measure body temperature and show the result on a small display, usually within several seconds to about a minute. They are used for oral, axillary and rectal readings in wards, clinics and emergency departments, and some models offer a faster predictive mode and memory of the last reading. Disposable probe covers are commonly used to prevent cross-contamination between patients. Normal values differ by measurement site, so record which site was used, and keep separate, clearly marked thermometers for rectal use.
products.specifications: Digital or infrared technology; °C/°F display; measurement range and accuracy vary by model; contact site or infrared measurement site specified by manufacturer; battery powered; disposable probe covers may be required for some contact systems.
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Infrared Thermometers
products.description: Infrared thermometers measure body temperature by detecting infrared energy emitted from the skin or eardrum, giving a reading in about a second. Forehead and temporal models work without contact or by scanning across the forehead, which helps with screening and with sleeping or uncooperative patients, while tympanic models read inside the ear canal, usually with a disposable probe cover. They are used in triage, wards, outpatient clinics and paediatric areas. Results can be affected by sweat, room temperature, earwax and technique, so let the device adjust to the room and follow the stated measuring distance and positioning.
products.specifications: Digital or infrared technology; °C/°F display; measurement range and accuracy vary by model; contact site or infrared measurement site specified by manufacturer; battery powered; disposable probe covers may be required for some contact systems.
products.precautions: Accuracy affected by ambient temperature and sweat/moisture on skin

products.name: ECG Monitors
products.description: ECG monitors continuously display and record the heart's electrical activity through skin electrodes, letting staff watch heart rate and rhythm and detect arrhythmias as they happen. Three-lead and five-lead configurations are used for ongoing rhythm monitoring in ICUs, wards, emergency departments and during transport, while 12-lead capability gives a fuller view for assessing ischaemia. Common features include heart-rate and arrhythmia alarms, ST-segment analysis on some models, trend storage and printing. Electrode placement and skin preparation strongly affect signal quality, so stock compatible disposable electrodes and lead sets for the patient sizes you treat.
products.specifications: Lead configurations: 3-, 5- or 12-lead; Display: colour screen with multiple waveform traces; Functions: heart-rate and arrhythmia alarms, ST analysis on some models; Recording: thermal printer or digital export on many models; Power: mains with battery backup
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Capnography Monitors
products.description: Capnography monitors measure carbon dioxide in exhaled breath and display it as an end-tidal CO2 value and a continuous waveform, giving breath-by-breath information on ventilation. They are used to confirm endotracheal tube placement, monitor ventilated patients and those under procedural sedation, and assess the effectiveness of CPR. Mainstream sensors sit directly in the airway circuit of intubated patients, while sidestream units draw a small gas sample through a disposable line, which also allows monitoring through nasal sampling cannulas in non-intubated patients. Sampling lines and airway adapters must match the monitor and patient size.
products.specifications: Measurement: EtCO2, respiratory rate, CO2 waveform; Technology: non-dispersive infrared; Sampling: mainstream or sidestream (approx. 50–200 mL/min); EtCO2 range: typically 0–99 mmHg or wider; Consumables: airway adapters, sampling lines, nasal CO2 cannulas
products.precautions: Confirms adequacy of ventilation, not oxygenation – use alongside SpO2 monitoring

products.name: Fetal Monitors
products.description: Fetal monitors, also called cardiotocographs, record fetal heart rate and uterine contractions to assess fetal well-being during pregnancy and labour. An ultrasound transducer detects the fetal heartbeat and a pressure (toco) transducer tracks contractions, both held on the abdomen with elastic belts and coupling gel, and many models add fetal movement marking and a printed or digital trace. Single and twin monitoring versions are available for antenatal clinics and labour wards. Reliable traces need correct transducer positioning and periodic confirmation that the recorded heart rate is fetal rather than maternal.
