products.specifications: Parameters: FHR (ultrasound), uterine activity (toco), fetal movement; Channels: single or twin FHR; Recording: thermal printer and/or digital storage; Options: maternal heart rate, SpO2 or NIBP on some models; Accessories: transducer belts, coupling gel
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Central Monitoring Systems
products.description: Central monitoring systems bring the waveforms, vital signs and alarms from many bedside monitors onto screens at a nursing station, so staff can observe several patients at once in ICUs, high-dependency units and step-down wards. They usually run on a workstation with one or more large displays connected to bedside and telemetry monitors over a wired or wireless network. Typical functions include full-disclosure review, trend and event storage, central alarm handling and printing or export to electronic records. Choose a system compatible with your existing bedside monitors and sized for the number of beds and data retention you need.
products.specifications: Capacity: multiple beds per station, model-dependent; Display: one or more large screens, multi-patient layout; Connectivity: wired LAN or wireless, bedside and telemetry monitors; Functions: central alarms, trends, full-disclosure review; Data: storage, printing, EMR interface on many models
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Stethoscopes
products.description: A stethoscope is a reusable acoustic diagnostic instrument used by clinicians to auscultate heart, lung, vascular and other body sounds. Common designs use a chestpiece with a diaphragm and/or bell connected to flexible tubing and binaural ear tips. Performance depends on chestpiece design, acoustic transmission, fit and maintenance.
products.specifications: Chestpiece: single- or dual-head; adult/pediatric options; diaphragm/bell configuration varies; stainless steel or other chestpiece materials; flexible tubing; replaceable ear tips and diaphragms may be available; overall length commonly around 60–70 cm, model-dependent.
products.precautions: Disinfect diaphragm and earpieces between patients

products.name: Otoscopes
products.description: Otoscopes are handheld instruments for examining the ear canal and eardrum, combining a light source, a magnifying lens and a cone-shaped speculum inserted into the ear. They are used in outpatient clinics, wards and emergency departments to assess ear infections, wax impaction, foreign bodies and eardrum perforation. Fibre-optic models carry light through the head for a bright, shadow-free view, and pneumatic versions let the examiner puff air to test eardrum mobility. Use the largest speculum that fits comfortably, with disposable specula to prevent cross-infection, and keep spare bulbs or batteries on hand.
products.specifications: Illumination: halogen, xenon or LED, direct or fibre-optic; Magnification: approx. 3x, swing-away lens on many models; Specula: reusable or disposable, approx. 2–5 mm tips; Power: battery handle or wall-mounted transformer; Options: pneumatic insufflation port
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Ophthalmoscopes
products.description: Direct ophthalmoscopes are handheld instruments that let clinicians look through the pupil at the retina, optic disc and blood vessels, and examine the lens and front structures of the eye. They are used in outpatient clinics, wards and emergency departments when assessing conditions such as diabetic and hypertensive retinopathy, papilloedema and cataract. A rotating lens wheel corrects for the refractive error of patient and examiner, and interchangeable apertures and filters, such as small spot, slit, grid and red-free, suit different pupil sizes and findings. Examination is easier in a darkened room, with dilated pupils when appropriate.
products.specifications: Type: direct, handheld; Lens wheel: wide diopter range, commonly about -20 to +20 D or more; Apertures: small/large spot, slit, grid, red-free filter; Illumination: halogen or LED; Power: rechargeable or dry-cell battery handle
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Diagnostic Sets
products.description: Diagnostic sets combine an otoscope head and an ophthalmoscope head on a shared battery handle, packed in a carry case so clinicians can examine ears, eyes and often the nose and throat with one kit. They are used in outpatient clinics, on ward rounds, in community visits and in teaching, where portability and quick switching between examinations matter. Sets typically include reusable and disposable ear specula, spare bulbs and sometimes a nasal speculum or throat illuminator. When choosing, check the bulb type, the handle's power source and whether heads and handles can be replaced individually.
products.specifications: Components: otoscope head, ophthalmoscope head, battery handle; Accessories: ear specula, spare bulbs, optional nasal speculum; Illumination: halogen, xenon or LED; Power: dry-cell or rechargeable handle; Storage: hard or soft carry case
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Examination Lamps
products.description: Examination lamps provide focused, adjustable light for physical examinations and minor procedures such as wound inspection, suturing, and gynaecological and ENT examinations. They come as mobile floor-stand models on castors, wall-mounted units and table-top versions, usually with a flexible gooseneck or articulated arm to position the beam. Most current lamps use LEDs, which give bright, cool light with little heat at the patient and a long service life. When selecting for a room, consider light intensity, spot size, colour rendering, the reach of the arm and how easily the head can be cleaned.
products.specifications: Light source: LED (halogen on older models); Colour temperature: approx. 4,000–5,000 K; Mounting: mobile stand, wall or table-top; Arm: gooseneck or articulated; Controls: on/off, dimming on many models
products.sizes: Mobile floor stand, wall-mounted, or table-top
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Aneroid Sphygmomanometers
products.description: Aneroid sphygmomanometers are manual blood pressure devices made up of an inflatable cuff, a hand bulb with release valve and a mechanical dial gauge, with readings taken by listening for Korotkoff sounds through a stethoscope. Being mercury-free and needing no power, they are used in outpatient clinics, wards and outreach work, and where automated readings may be unreliable, such as in irregular heart rhythms. Palm-held, desk and clip-on gauges are available with adult, large adult and paediatric cuffs. The needle should rest at zero before inflation, and gauges should be checked regularly, as they can drift, especially after being dropped.
products.specifications: Automated or manual measurement; adult, large-adult, pediatric and neonatal cuff options; pressure measurement range and accuracy vary; memory, averaging, alarms and connectivity vary on electronic models; cuff sizes must match patient arm circumference.
products.precautions: Requires periodic calibration against a reference standard

products.name: Digital BP Monitors
products.description: Digital BP monitors are automatic devices that inflate the cuff, sense pressure oscillations in the artery and display systolic and diastolic pressure and pulse rate on a screen, with no stethoscope needed. Upper-arm models are preferred in clinical settings, while wrist models are more compact; many store readings, average several measurements and flag irregular heartbeats. They suit outpatient triage, ward rounds and home monitoring programmes. Accuracy depends on the correct cuff size, keeping the arm at heart level and a rested patient, and oscillometric readings can be unreliable in some arrhythmias.
products.specifications: Method: oscillometric; Cuff pressure range: approx. 0–299 mmHg; Pulse range: approx. 40–180 bpm; Memory: stored readings, multi-user on some models; Cuffs: adult, large adult, paediatric; Power: batteries and/or AC adapter
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Wall-Mounted BP Monitors
products.description: Wall-mounted BP monitors are fixed blood pressure units installed in examination rooms, triage bays and ward areas, keeping the gauge at eye level and the cuff always at hand. Most are aneroid units with a large dial on a wall bracket, a coiled tube and a basket to hold the cuff, though digital wall-mounted models also exist. Because they cannot be dropped or misplaced, they tend to hold calibration longer and save bench space in busy rooms. Mount them at a convenient height beside the examination couch and check that the tubing reaches the patient's arm both sitting and lying.
products.specifications: Type: aneroid dial, digital models available; Scale: 0–300 mmHg; Dial: large face for reading at a distance; Mounting: wall bracket with cuff basket and coiled tubing; Cuffs: adult, large adult
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Pediatric BP Monitors
products.description: Pediatric BP monitors are blood pressure devices set up for neonates, infants and children, using smaller cuffs and, on automated models, inflation pressures and measurement settings adapted to small arms and faster heart rates. They are used in paediatric wards, NICUs and outpatient clinics, either as manual aneroid sets with a range of child cuffs or as automated oscillometric monitors with paediatric and neonatal modes. Cuff choice is critical: the bladder width should be about 40 percent of the arm circumference, as a cuff that is too large or too small gives falsely low or high readings. Select the patient mode matching the child's age and size.
products.specifications: Patient age/weight range, dimensions, measurement ranges, alarms, materials and accessories vary by model; pediatric/neonatal sizing must match the manufacturer's specified patient population.
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Blood Glucose Meters
products.description: Blood glucose meters are handheld devices that measure glucose in a small drop of capillary blood applied to a disposable test strip, giving a result within seconds. In hospitals and clinics they are used for point-of-care monitoring of patients with diabetes, during insulin infusions and for screening, and they are also used for home self-monitoring. Most strips use an enzyme-based electrochemical method needing only about 0.3 to 1 microlitre of blood, obtained with a sterile single-use lancet. Use strips matched to the meter, check their expiry dates and run control solutions regularly, since hematocrit and some substances can affect results.
products.specifications: Method: electrochemical, glucose oxidase or dehydrogenase strips; Sample: approx. 0.3–1 µL capillary whole blood; Measuring range: approx. 20–600 mg/dL (1.1–33.3 mmol/L); Test time: approx. 5–10 s; Consumables: test strips, sterile lancets, control solution
products.precautions: Requires periodic control-solution/quality checks; strips are lot- and meter-specific

products.name: Hemoglobin Analyzers
products.description: Hemoglobin analyzers are compact point-of-care devices that measure haemoglobin concentration from a single drop of capillary or venous blood, drawn into a disposable microcuvette or applied to a test strip and read photometrically, usually within about a minute. They are used for anaemia screening in outpatient and antenatal clinics, blood donor selection and wards where a quick result helps before full laboratory testing. Many are battery-operated and portable for outreach work. Good capillary sampling technique matters, as squeezing the finger hard or using the first drop can dilute the sample with tissue fluid and give falsely low results.
products.specifications: Method: photometric or reflectance; Sample: approx. 10 µL capillary or venous blood; Measuring range: approx. 0–25 g/dL; Test time: under about 60 s; Consumables: microcuvettes or strips, sterile lancets; Power: battery or mains
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Urine Analyzers
products.description: Urine analyzers are benchtop instruments that read urine reagent strips automatically by reflectance photometry, removing the subjectivity of judging colour changes by eye. A dipped strip is placed on the tray and the analyzer reports parameters such as glucose, protein, blood, leukocytes, nitrite, ketones, pH and specific gravity, then prints or stores the result. They are used in outpatient clinics, wards and laboratories for routine urinalysis and screening. Each analyzer reads only compatible strip types, so check ongoing strip supply and cost, and follow the dipping, blotting and timing steps exactly for consistent results.
products.specifications: Method: reflectance photometry; Parameters: up to approx. 10–14 per strip; Throughput: dozens to several hundred strips per hour; Output: built-in printer, USB or LIS connection on many models; Consumables: compatible reagent strips, calibration strips
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Hematology Analyzers
products.description: Hematology analyzers are automated laboratory instruments that perform a complete blood count from a small sample of anticoagulated whole blood, reporting red cells, white cells, platelets, haemoglobin, haematocrit and red cell indices. Three-part differential models sort white cells into lymphocytes, mid-sized cells and granulocytes by impedance, while five-part models add optical or flow-based methods to separate neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils and basophils. They rely on reagents, diluents and controls as ongoing consumables. Choose between 3-part and 5-part according to workload and clinical needs, and factor in reagent use, quality control and maintenance.
products.specifications: Differential: 3-part or 5-part WBC; Sample: approx. 10–150 µL EDTA whole blood; Technology: impedance, plus optical/flow cytometry on 5-part; Throughput: approx. 30–100+ samples per hour; Data: QC software, LIS connectivity
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Chemistry Analyzers
products.description: Chemistry analyzers are laboratory instruments that measure substances in serum, plasma or urine, such as glucose, lipids, kidney and liver function markers, electrolytes and enzymes. They mix sample and reagent, incubate the reaction and read it photometrically, and some add ion-selective electrodes for sodium, potassium and chloride. Semi-automated benchtop models suit smaller laboratories, while fully automated systems handle larger test menus and higher throughput with walk-away operation. Selection depends on daily test volume, the test menu needed, reagent availability, open versus closed reagent systems, and water, power and maintenance requirements.
products.specifications: Type: semi-automated or fully automated; Method: photometric, optional ISE for Na/K/Cl; Sample types: serum, plasma, urine; Throughput: low to several hundred tests per hour, model-dependent; Reagents: open or closed system; Data: LIS connectivity
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Oxygen Concentrators
products.description: Oxygen concentrators draw in room air and pass it through molecular sieve beds that remove nitrogen, delivering oxygen-enriched gas continuously without the need for cylinders. They are used for long-term oxygen therapy at home, in wards and clinics, and as a supplementary supply where piped oxygen is limited. Stationary units typically provide continuous flow from about 1 to 10 L/min, while portable models often use pulse-dose delivery. Purity generally falls as flow increases, so match the rated flow to the prescription, and plan for a reliable power supply, filter cleaning, space around the unit and a backup cylinder.
products.specifications: Oxygen concentration commonly specified around 90–96% depending on flow and model; continuous-flow models commonly offer approximately 1–10 L/min, while high-flow units may provide more; outlet pressure, power consumption, noise, alarms, operating altitude and battery/backup capability vary by model.
products.precautions: Requires stable mains power; not for use near open flame; check altitude derating
products.useSetting: ICU, wards, emergency department, home care

products.name: Oxygen Cylinders
products.description: Medical oxygen cylinders are high-pressure containers used to store and transport medical oxygen for patient therapy, emergency response and clinical procedures. They are commonly connected to an approved regulator and flowmeter. Cylinder selection requires consideration of gas purity/service, water capacity, working pressure, valve configuration, portability and applicable pressure-vessel requirements.
products.specifications: Medical oxygen service; cylinder material may be aluminium or steel; water capacity and working pressure vary by cylinder; valve standard depends on market; compatible regulator required; hydrostatic/periodic inspection requirements depend on jurisdiction and cylinder type.
products.sizes: Common sizes: B/C/D/E, up to large H/J cylinders
products.precautions: High-pressure vessel – secure upright, away from heat; oxidiser hazard
products.useSetting: ICU, wards, emergency department, home care

products.name: Oxygen Regulators
products.description: Oxygen regulators attach to an oxygen cylinder valve and reduce the high cylinder pressure to a safe, steady low pressure for patient delivery. Most combine a contents gauge showing cylinder pressure with a click-style flow selector or flowmeter, and connect through a pin-index yoke or a threaded fitting depending on the valve type. They are used with portable cylinders for patient transport, emergency trolleys, ambulances and home care. Choose a regulator that matches the cylinder valve and required flow range, open the cylinder valve slowly, and keep the regulator free of oil and grease, which can ignite in high-pressure oxygen.
products.specifications: Inlet: pin-index yoke or threaded, matched to cylinder valve; Inlet rating: typical medical cylinder pressures (approx. 150–200+ bar); Flow: click-style approx. 0–15 L/min or flowmeter outlet; Gauge: cylinder contents gauge; Body: brass or aluminium
products.precautions: Verify regulator is oxygen-cylinder-compatible (pin index/thread) before connecting
products.useSetting: ICU, wards, emergency department, home care

products.name: Oxygen Flowmeters
products.description: Oxygen flowmeters control and display the rate of oxygen delivered to a patient, connecting to a wall outlet on a piped gas system or to a regulated cylinder. Thorpe-tube models have a clear tube with a floating ball read against a scale, while dial or click-style models offer preset flow steps. A range of 0–15 L/min is common, with low-flow versions for neonates and paediatrics. They are often fitted with a humidifier bottle when supplying masks and cannulas. Thorpe tubes must be mounted upright to read correctly, and the inlet probe must match the facility's wall-outlet type.
products.specifications: Type: Thorpe tube (float) or click/dial; Range: 0–15 L/min standard, low-flow ranges available; Inlet: wall-outlet probe or threaded, matched to system; Outlet: barbed nipple or humidifier connection; Body: polycarbonate tube with metal housing
products.precautions: Low-flow (paediatric) flowmeters needed for infants – do not use standard flowmeter
products.useSetting: ICU, wards, emergency department, home care

products.name: Oxygen Masks
products.description: Oxygen masks deliver supplemental oxygen through a soft, clear mask covering the nose and mouth, connected by tubing to an oxygen source. Simple masks give moderate concentrations at medium flows, venturi masks use colour-coded adapters to deliver a set and more precise oxygen percentage, and non-rebreather masks with a reservoir bag and one-way valves provide high concentrations in emergencies. They are disposable, single-patient devices in adult and paediatric sizes. Run each type within its recommended flow range: simple masks need enough flow to flush out exhaled carbon dioxide, and a non-rebreather's reservoir bag should stay inflated.
products.specifications: Adult/pediatric/neonatal sizes; nasal cannula, simple mask, non-rebreather and other designs vary; tubing length and connector vary; recommended flow range is interface-specific.
products.sizes: Adult and paediatric; simple, venturi, non-rebreather variants
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: ICU, wards, emergency department, home care

products.name: Nasal Cannulas
products.description: Nasal cannulas are lightweight tubes with two short prongs that sit just inside the nostrils to deliver low-flow supplemental oxygen while leaving the mouth free for eating, drinking and talking. The tubing loops over the ears and adjusts under the chin, and soft, curved prongs aid comfort during long-term use. They are disposable and made in adult, paediatric and neonatal sizes for wards, ICUs, emergency departments and home oxygen. Standard cannulas are generally run at about 1 to 6 L/min in adults; higher flows dry the nasal lining, so humidification or a high-flow system is used when more oxygen is needed.
products.specifications: Adult/pediatric/neonatal sizes; nasal cannula, simple mask, non-rebreather and other designs vary; tubing length and connector vary; recommended flow range is interface-specific.
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: ICU, wards, emergency department, home care

products.name: CPAP Machines
products.description: CPAP machines deliver continuous positive airway pressure through a mask to keep the upper airway open, and are mainly used to treat obstructive sleep apnoea in sleep clinics and at home, with some use in hospital respiratory care. Fixed-pressure devices hold one prescribed pressure, while auto-titrating models adjust within a set range, typically 4–20 cmH2O, as breathing changes. Most offer ramp settings, heated humidification and recording of usage and leak data. Mask fit strongly affects comfort and adherence, so nasal, nasal pillow and full-face options should be available, with tubing and cushions cleaned and replaced regularly.
products.specifications: Pressure range and operating modes vary by model; humidifier compatibility; leak compensation; ramp and comfort settings; patient interface compatibility; data storage/connectivity; alarms and backup-battery capability vary.
products.sizes: Fixed or auto-titrating pressure, 4–20 cmH2O typical range
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: BiPAP Machines
products.description: BiPAP machines, or bilevel positive airway pressure devices, deliver two pressures: a higher inspiratory pressure (IPAP) to assist each breath and a lower expiratory pressure (EPAP) to keep the airway open. This suits them to non-invasive ventilation in conditions such as COPD exacerbations, hypercapnic respiratory failure, neuromuscular disease and sleep apnoea not tolerated on CPAP. Pressures typically span about 4 to 25 cmH2O, with spontaneous, timed and spontaneous/timed modes providing a backup breath rate. Hospital units add alarms and monitoring; a well-fitted full-face or nasal mask is essential, as leaks reduce effective support.
products.specifications: Pressure range and operating modes vary by model; humidifier compatibility; leak compensation; ramp and comfort settings; patient interface compatibility; data storage/connectivity; alarms and backup-battery capability vary.
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: ICU, wards, emergency department, home care

products.name: Ventilators
products.description: Ventilators are machines that mechanically move air and oxygen into and out of the lungs for patients who cannot breathe adequately on their own, either through an endotracheal or tracheostomy tube or non-invasively with a mask. ICU ventilators offer a full range of volume, pressure and spontaneous modes with detailed monitoring, while transport and portable units are smaller, battery-powered and suited to transfers and emergencies. Adult, paediatric and neonatal capability depends on the model. Selection should consider the patient population, required modes, gas supply, battery runtime and the availability of compatible circuits, filters and humidifiers.
products.specifications: Ventilation modes vary; tidal-volume and pressure ranges are model-specific; adjustable FiO2 and PEEP; respiratory-rate control; inspiratory-flow and pressure monitoring; configurable alarms; humidification compatibility; mains and battery operation; data export/connectivity vary.
products.sizes: Adult, paediatric, neonatal modes; portable to ICU-grade
products.precautions: Requires trained operator, backup power, and regular circuit/filter changes
products.useSetting: ICU, wards, emergency department, home care

products.name: High-Flow Oxygen Systems
products.description: High-flow oxygen systems deliver heated, humidified air-oxygen mixtures at up to 60 L/min through wide-bore nasal cannulas, with oxygen concentration set independently of flow. The high flow matches or exceeds the patient's own inspiratory demand, flushes carbon dioxide from the upper airway and adds a small positive pressure, while warmth and humidity improve comfort and help clear secretions. They are used for acute hypoxaemic respiratory failure, after extubation and in emergency and ward settings. Cannula prongs should fill no more than about half of each nostril so that gas can escape around them.
products.specifications: Flow range: up to approx. 60 L/min adult, lower paediatric ranges; FiO2: approx. 21–100%, adjustable; Humidification: heated, approx. 31–37°C; Interface: wide-bore nasal cannula or tracheostomy adapter; Consumables: heated circuit, humidifier chamber
products.sizes: Up to 60 L/min heated, humidified flow
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: ICU, wards, emergency department, home care

products.name: Nebulizers
products.description: Nebulizers convert liquid medication into a fine mist inhaled through a mask or mouthpiece, delivering bronchodilators, steroids, antibiotics or saline directly to the airways. Compressor or jet nebulizers are robust and economical but noisier, vibrating-mesh units are quiet, portable and leave less medication behind, and ultrasonic models are quiet but not suitable for every drug. They are used in emergency departments, wards, clinics and at home, especially for children and patients who struggle with inhalers. Medication cups, masks and tubing should be cleaned and dried after each use or replaced to prevent contamination.

products.name: Endotracheal Tubes
products.description: Endotracheal tubes are sterile, single-use tubes passed through the mouth or nose into the trachea to secure the airway, allow mechanical ventilation and protect the lungs from aspiration. They are usually clear PVC with a radiopaque line, depth markings and a Murphy eye, and come cuffed, with a high-volume low-pressure cuff and pilot balloon, or uncuffed. Sizes run from 2.5 mm internal diameter for neonates to about 9.0 mm for large adults, with variants such as reinforced, preformed oral or nasal, and subglottic suction tubes. Cuff pressure should be checked regularly to avoid leaks or tracheal injury.

products.name: Tracheostomy Tubes

They come cuffed or uncuffed, with or without a removable inner cannula for cleaning, and in fenestrated versions that can allow speech when appropriate, with a neck flange and ties holding the tube in place. Most are sterile single-use PVC or silicone tubes from neonatal to adult sizes, with some reusable metal variants. Sizing should consider both internal diameter and length to suit neck anatomy.

products.name: Laryngeal Masks
products.description: Laryngeal masks are supraglottic airway devices with an inflatable cuff that sits over the laryngeal inlet, attached to an airway tube that exits through the mouth, providing a clear airway without entering the trachea. They are widely used for shorter anaesthetic procedures and as a rescue airway when face-mask ventilation or intubation is difficult. Sizes run from 1 for neonates to 5 for large adults, chosen mainly by body weight. Most are sterile single-use PVC devices, while reusable silicone versions can be reprocessed a limited number of times. Classic designs do not reliably protect against aspiration, so patient selection matters.

products.name: Supraglottic Airways

They are used in anaesthesia, emergency and pre-hospital care, and resuscitation as a quick-to-insert airway when intubation is unnecessary or has failed, and some designs act as a conduit for passing an endotracheal tube. These sterile, single-use devices come in sizes 1 to 5, selected by patient weight. Designs with a drain tube give better protection against gastric inflation and regurgitation.

products.description: Ambu bags, also called bag-valve-mask resuscitators, are hand-squeezed self-inflating bags used to ventilate patients who are not breathing or are breathing inadequately, during CPR, before intubation and in transport. A set typically includes the bag, a non-rebreathing patient valve, a face mask and an oxygen reservoir, with a pressure-relief valve common on paediatric and neonatal sizes. Reusable silicone versions are reprocessed between patients, while single-patient-use versions are also widely used. Choose bag volume by patient size, add a PEEP valve when needed, and squeeze only enough to make the chest rise, avoiding over-ventilation.

Components are individually sterile-packed where required, and adult and paediatric configurations are available. Kits should be checked on a set schedule for completeness, expiry dates and, where included, laryngoscope light function.

products.description: Surgical scissors are precision cutting instruments for cutting tissue, sutures, dressings and other materials during operations and minor procedures. Common patterns include Metzenbaum scissors for delicate tissue dissection, Mayo scissors for heavier tissue and fascia, iris scissors for fine work and suture scissors for stitches, in straight or curved forms and lengths of about 11 to 23 cm. Tips may be sharp/sharp, sharp/blunt or blunt/blunt, and tungsten carbide inserts help blades stay sharp longer. Reusable stainless steel scissors are cleaned and sterilized between uses and should be inspected for sharpness and alignment; sterile single-use versions are also available.

products.name: Surgical Forceps
products.description: Surgical forceps are instruments used to grasp, hold and manipulate tissue, dressings and swabs during operations and minor procedures. Thumb forceps, such as tissue and dressing forceps, are held like a pencil and work by spring tension; toothed tips give a secure grip on tougher tissue like skin, while non-toothed tips handle delicate tissue and vessels. Ring-handled forceps, such as artery and sponge-holding forceps, lock with a ratchet to clamp or hold. They range from about 10 to 25 cm in stainless steel for reprocessing between uses. Inspect tips for alignment and wear, as damaged teeth can crush or slip on tissue.

products.name: Hemostatic Forceps
products.description: Hemostatic forceps, often called artery forceps or haemostats, are locking surgical instruments used to clamp blood vessels and control bleeding during open procedures. A ratchet lock between the finger rings holds the jaws closed so the surgeon's hands are free, and serrated jaws grip tissue without slipping. Common patterns include the fine-tipped Mosquito, the mid-sized Kelly and the longer Rochester-Pean, in straight or curved forms from about 12.5cm to 20cm. Choose length and jaw delicacy to suit vessel size and wound depth, and inspect ratchets and jaw alignment after each reprocessing cycle.

products.name: Needle Holders
products.description: Needle holders, also called needle drivers, are locking instruments that grip a curved suture needle firmly while the surgeon passes it through tissue. Compared with hemostats they have shorter, heavier jaws, often with a cross-hatched or tungsten carbide insert that stops the needle rotating. Patterns range from the general-purpose Mayo-Hegar to finer Webster or Crile-Wood holders, in lengths of roughly 12cm to 20cm. Match jaw size to needle size, since a fine needle clamped in a heavy jaw can bend or flatten, and check the jaw surface for wear during reprocessing.

products.name: Retractors
products.description: Surgical retractors hold back skin, muscle and organs so the surgeon has a clear view of and access to the operative field. Hand-held types such as Langenbeck, Senn, Army-Navy and Deaver retractors are held by an assistant and repositioned as needed, while self-retaining types such as Weitlaner, Gelpi and Balfour retractors lock open with a ratchet or screw and free up staff. Blades come in different widths, depths and tip shapes, from smooth blades to sharp or blunt pronged rakes. Select blade depth and width for the incision, and use blunt blades near vessels and nerves.

Many have longer or specially shaped jaws compared with fine hemostats, such as atraumatic intestinal clamps with longitudinal serrations, crushing clamps for tissue that will be resected, right-angle clamps for dissecting around structures, and towel clamps for draping. They are available straight or curved in various jaw lengths. Choose atraumatic jaws whenever the clamped tissue must remain viable after the clamp is removed.

The No.3 handle fits smaller blades such as No.10, 11, 12 and 15 for fine and general incisions, while the larger No.4 handle takes No.20 to 24 blades for longer incisions through thicker tissue. Long-shaft versions of the No.3 are available for deep cavities. Handles usually have a ribbed or knurled grip for control. Mount and remove blades with a needle holder or blade remover rather than fingers to reduce the risk of sharps injuries.

The No.10 has a curved edge for general skin incisions, the No.11 is a pointed triangular blade for stab incisions and drainage, the No.12 is hooked for suture removal and confined spaces, and the small curved No.15 gives precise, short cuts. The larger No.20 and 22 fit the No.4 handle for long incisions. Each blade is individually foil-packed and should be discarded straight into a sharps container after use.

Most general-purpose hospital units offer both monopolar output, used with a handpiece and a patient return electrode, and bipolar output, used with forceps that pass current only between their tips. Cut, blend and coagulation modes are selected on the front panel, with power adjustable up to around 300W. When choosing a unit, check return-electrode monitoring, alarm functions and compatibility with the pencils, forceps and pads already in use.

This makes them suited to cutting and coagulating over larger areas in general, orthopaedic and plastic surgery. Typical modes include pure cut, blended cut and several coagulation settings, with power adjustable from about 1W to 300W. Because current crosses the body, correct return-pad placement and caution around implanted devices are essential, and return-electrode quality monitoring helps reduce burn risk.

This gives precise, low-power coagulation for delicate work in neurosurgery, ophthalmic, ENT, hand and microsurgery, and near nerves or implanted devices. Power output is adjustable and usually far lower than monopolar settings. Units may be activated by footswitch or by auto-bipolar tissue sensing, and some support irrigating forceps that reduce tissue sticking to the tips.

Extended-length tips reach deep cavities, and coated tips reduce charred tissue build-up. Confirm the connector matches the generator before ordering.

Split-pad designs work with return-electrode monitoring to alarm when contact becomes poor. Adult and paediatric sizes are available; the adhesive surface is single-use, and pads should never be cut or repositioned.

products.name: Defibrillators
products.description: Defibrillators deliver a controlled electric shock to the heart to treat life-threatening rhythms such as ventricular fibrillation and pulseless ventricular tachycardia. Hospital units usually combine a manual mode, where the clinician reads the ECG and selects energy, with an AED mode, and many add synchronised cardioversion, transcutaneous pacing and ECG monitoring. Energy is typically selectable from about 1J to 360J, with biphasic waveforms now common, delivered through paddles or disposable adhesive pads. Check pacing capability, battery type, event recording and paediatric pad availability.
products.specifications: Device type: AED/manual/manual-AED combination; biphasic waveform common; selectable or automated energy levels vary; ECG monitoring options vary; adult/pediatric pads; rechargeable or replaceable battery; event recording and data transfer vary.
products.precautions: Requires regular self-test/battery checks; clear personnel before shock delivery

products.name: AEDs
products.description: Automated external defibrillators (AEDs) analyse the heart rhythm through adhesive chest pads and advise or deliver a shock when a shockable rhythm such as ventricular fibrillation is detected. Voice and visual prompts guide the rescuer through pad placement, CPR and shock delivery, so trained laypersons and first responders can act before a clinical team arrives. Semi-automatic models ask the user to press a shock button, fully automatic models shock without input, and protocols use fixed or escalating energy. Plan for pad and battery expiry and a visible, accessible wall cabinet.
products.specifications: Device type: AED/manual/manual-AED combination; biphasic waveform common; selectable or automated energy levels vary; ECG monitoring options vary; adult/pediatric pads; rechargeable or replaceable battery; event recording and data transfer vary.
products.sizes: Fixed energy or escalating shock protocols
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Emergency Carts
products.description: Emergency carts, or crash carts, are lockable multi-drawer trolleys that keep resuscitation drugs, airway equipment, IV supplies and a defibrillator together for cardiac arrest and other emergencies. The top surface typically holds the defibrillator or monitor, with a CPR board on the back and an IV pole and oxygen cylinder holder at the side. Drawers are often colour-coded or labelled by function, and numbered breakaway seals show whether stock has been opened. Standardise drawer layout across units so staff can find items quickly under pressure.
products.specifications: Drawers: typically 4–6, lockable or seal-secured; Construction: steel, aluminium or ABS plastic; Accessories: IV pole, CPR board, oxygen holder, defibrillator shelf; Mobility: casters with brakes; Security: central lock or breakaway seals
products.precautions: Requires daily/shift checklist and lock/seal system to confirm contents are complete

products.name: CPR Boards
products.description: CPR boards are rigid backboards placed under a patient lying on a soft bed or mattress so chest compressions push on the chest rather than sinking into the mattress. Half-body boards fit beneath the torso and slide in quickly during an in-hospital arrest, while full-body boards also support the head and pelvis. They are usually moulded plastic or composite with handgrips, and are often mounted on the back of a crash cart. Look for a lightweight, X-ray translucent board that is easy to wipe down and disinfect.
products.specifications: Types: half-body and full-body; Material: moulded plastic or composite; Features: handholds, radiolucent options; Mounting: brackets for crash carts or walls; Cleaning: wipe-clean, disinfectant compatible
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Resuscitation Kits
products.description: Resuscitation kits bring together the disposable supplies needed to manage airway and breathing during a cardiac or respiratory arrest. A typical kit includes a bag-valve-mask resuscitator with oxygen reservoir, face masks in several sizes, oropharyngeal airways, oxygen tubing and suction catheters, with some versions adding IV cannulas and syringes. Components are individually sterile-packed and grouped in a carry case or sealed pouch. Adult and paediatric configurations differ in bag, mask and airway size, so stock the correct kit for each care area and check expiry dates regularly.

products.name: Cervical Collars
products.description: Cervical collars support the neck and limit movement of the cervical spine when a spinal injury is suspected. Rigid extrication collars used in emergency care come in fixed sizes, from no-neck and short to regular, tall and paediatric, or as one adjustable collar that sets to several heights. Most have a front opening for pulse checks and airway access. Soft foam collars give comfort rather than true immobilisation. Size by measuring the neck carefully, since a poorly fitted collar may not restrict movement and can compromise the airway.

products.name: Spine Boards
products.description: Spine boards, or long backboards, are rigid flat boards used to move a patient with a suspected spinal injury while keeping the head, neck and trunk aligned. The patient is log-rolled onto the board and secured with straps and a head immobiliser. Modern boards are moulded polyethylene, X-ray translucent and often buoyant for water rescue, with multiple handholds and strap pins. Standard boards suit adults, with paediatric versions available. Boards are intended mainly for extrication and transfer, so time spent lying on one should be kept short.

products.name: Splints
products.description: Splints immobilise suspected fractures, dislocations and soft-tissue injuries to reduce pain and prevent further damage during assessment and transport. Common types include mouldable foam-padded aluminium splints that can be shaped to any limb, rigid arm and leg boards, finger splints, and inflatable air splints that apply even pressure around the limb. Most are single-patient-use, though rigid versions can be cleaned and reused. Immobilise the joints above and below the injury, and check circulation, sensation and movement beyond the splint after applying it.

products.name: Immobilization Devices
products.description: Immobilization devices hold an injured patient's head, spine and body in position during extrication, transport and imaging. Head blocks attach to a spine board or stretcher to stop the head turning, vacuum mattresses mould around the body and become rigid when air is drawn out, and vest-type extrication devices stabilise the head and torso of a seated patient trapped in a vehicle. Most are made of washable, radiolucent materials and fastened with colour-coded straps. Choose devices that fit existing boards and stretchers, and check vacuum mattresses for leaks.

products.name: Trauma Kits
products.description: Trauma kits assemble the supplies needed to control bleeding and manage injuries at the scene, in transit or in the emergency department. Contents commonly include tourniquets, pressure and haemostatic dressings, trauma bandages, gauze, shears, gloves, chest seals and airway adjuncts, with components individually sterile-packed where required. Sizes range from compact individual first-responder pouches to large bags stocked for multiple casualties. Choose a kit by the number of patients and the injury types expected, and log used or expiring items so they are replaced.

products.name: ICU Patient Monitors
products.description: ICU patient monitors continuously display and record vital signs for critically ill patients and alarm when values cross set limits. Beyond standard ECG, SpO2, non-invasive blood pressure, respiration and temperature, ICU models commonly add invasive pressure channels for arterial and central venous lines, capnography and cardiac output measurement, often through plug-in modules. Large touchscreens show waveforms and trends, and units can network to a central station for remote viewing. Check the number of parameter slots, arrhythmia analysis features and compatibility with existing central systems.

products.name: Infusion Pumps
products.description: Volumetric infusion pumps deliver IV fluids, medicines and blood products at a programmed rate and volume through an administration set. They are used when a gravity drip is not accurate enough, such as for continuous drug infusions, fluid balance in the ICU or timed infusions on wards. Rates typically range from 0.1 to 999 mL/h, with alarms for air-in-line, occlusion, door open and infusion complete, and many models include drug libraries with dose limits. Confirm which administration sets the pump accepts, since dedicated sets add ongoing consumable cost.
products.specifications: Flow-rate range, bolus function, occlusion pressure, accuracy, syringe/set compatibility, alarm types, drug library, event logging and connectivity vary by model; mains and rechargeable battery operation common.
products.precautions: Free-flow protection and correct set loading are critical to avoid dosing errors

products.name: Syringe Pumps
products.description: Syringe pumps drive the plunger of a loaded syringe at a precise, steady rate, making them suited to small-volume, high-concentration infusions such as vasopressors, sedation, insulin and neonatal medicines. They accept standard syringes of about 5mL to 60mL and deliver rates typically from 0.1 to 1200 mL/h, with bolus, purge and occlusion alarm functions. The syringe size and type must be correctly set or recognised for accurate delivery. Check which syringe brands and sizes are calibrated on the pump before standardising supplies.
products.specifications: Flow-rate range, bolus function, occlusion pressure, accuracy, syringe/set compatibility, alarm types, drug library, event logging and connectivity vary by model; mains and rechargeable battery operation common.
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Feeding Pumps
products.description: Enteral feeding pumps deliver liquid nutrition through a nasogastric, nasojejunal or gastrostomy tube at a controlled rate when patients cannot eat enough by mouth. They are used in ICU and wards for continuous or intermittent feeding, typically at 1 to 300 mL/h, and many can also schedule water flushes. Dedicated enteral sets with non-luer connectors help prevent feed being connected to an IV line by mistake. Alarms cover occlusion, empty bag and low battery. Check set compatibility, portability for mobile patients and ease of cleaning.
products.specifications: Rate: typically 1–300 mL/h; Modes: continuous, intermittent, water flush; Sets: dedicated enteral sets with enteral-only connectors; Alarms: occlusion, feed empty, low battery; Power: mains and rechargeable battery; Mounting: IV pole clamp
products.precautions: Enteral-only connectors (ENFit) reduce risk of IV misconnection

products.name: IV Administration Sets
products.description: IV administration sets connect a fluid bag or bottle to a patient's cannula or catheter for gravity infusion or use with a pump. Each set includes a spike, a drip chamber, tubing, a roller clamp for rate control, an injection port and a luer connector. Standard macro-drip sets deliver about 20 drops per mL for routine fluids, while micro-drip sets deliver about 60 drops per mL for precise low-volume or paediatric infusions. Some include an air vent for rigid bottles or an in-line filter. Always confirm the drop factor before calculating drip rates.

products.name: IV Extension Sets
products.description: IV extension sets add length or extra access points between an IV catheter and the main administration line. Extra length lets patients move without pulling on the cannula, and short extensions keep line changes away from the insertion site, reducing manipulation of the catheter hub. Sets come in various lengths with single or multiple lumens, with or without injection ports, slide or pinch clamps and needle-free connectors. Small-bore versions keep dead volume low for syringe pump use. Match connector type and priming volume to the infusion.

products.name: IV Fluids
products.description: IV fluids are sterile solutions given directly into a vein to replace fluid and electrolytes, maintain hydration and act as a carrier for diluted medicines. Common types include 0.9% sodium chloride, lactated Ringer's, dextrose solutions in water or saline, and other balanced electrolyte solutions. They come in flexible bags or bottles from about 50mL, used for drug dilution, up to 1000mL for fluid replacement. The choice of solution and volume is a prescribing decision; for supply, check container type, port design and compatibility with administration sets.

products.name: Disposable Syringes
products.description: Disposable syringes are sterile, single-use plastic syringes used to draw up and inject medicines, flush lines and collect samples. They range from 1mL for small doses to 50–60mL for feeds, irrigation and syringe pumps. Tips may be luer slip, where the needle pushes on, or luer lock, which screws on securely and is preferred for pumps and pressurised injections; larger syringes are also made with catheter tips. Most have a clear polypropylene barrel and rubber plunger seal. Choose the smallest syringe that holds the dose for easier reading of graduations.

products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Insulin Syringes
products.description: Insulin syringes are small-volume syringes with a fine 30G or 31G needle permanently attached for subcutaneous insulin injection. Barrels are graduated in insulin units rather than millilitres: the 0.3mL size holds up to 30 units, 0.5mL up to 50 units and 1mL up to 100 units of U-100 insulin. The fixed needle leaves very little dead space, so little insulin is wasted. Choose the smallest barrel that fits the dose for easier, more accurate reading, and make sure the syringe calibration matches the insulin concentration in use.

products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Safety Syringes
products.description: Safety syringes include a built-in mechanism that covers or withdraws the needle after injection to help prevent needlestick injuries and reuse. Retractable designs pull the needle into the barrel when the plunger is fully depressed, while shielded designs use a hinged or sliding sheath that locks over the needle. Auto-disable versions also lock the plunger after one use so the syringe cannot be refilled. Sizes typically range from 1mL to 10mL. Prefer mechanisms that activate one-handed and fit routine injection technique, and train staff before introduction.
products.specifications: Sizes: 1–10mL; Mechanism: retractable needle, sliding or hinged shield, auto-disable; Activation: one-handed on many designs; Needle: attached, or luer fitting for separate safety needles; Packaging: sterile, single use
products.precautions: Reduces but does not eliminate needlestick risk – activate safety mechanism immediately after use

products.name: Hypodermic Needles
products.description: Hypodermic needles are sterile single-use needles that attach to a syringe through a luer hub for injections, drawing up medicines and aspirating fluid. Gauge sets the bore: 18G and 19G suit drawing up and viscous fluids, 21G to 23G suit intramuscular injections and venepuncture, and 25G to 27G suit intradermal and subcutaneous injections. Lengths range from about 13mm to 38mm, and hubs are colour-coded by gauge for quick identification. Select length according to injection route and patient size, and keep a sharps container at the point of use.

products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Blood Collection Needles
products.description: Blood collection needles are designed for venepuncture, either as double-ended needles that screw into a tube holder for evacuated tube systems, or as winged butterfly sets with flexible tubing for small, fragile or hard-to-reach veins. Gauges of 21G to 23G balance sample flow against patient comfort, with 21G common for routine adult draws and 23G for children and difficult veins. Many include a safety shield that covers the needle after use. Confirm compatibility with the tube holders and tubes in use, and use a discard tube with butterfly sets when coagulation tubes are drawn first.

products.name: Centrifuges
products.description: A laboratory centrifuge separates components of blood, urine and other specimens by applying centrifugal force. The required rotor type, speed and relative centrifugal force depend on the application. Safety features and balancing procedures are important for reliable operation and operator protection.

products.name: Microscopes
products.description: Laboratory microscopes are compound light microscopes used to examine blood smears, urine sediment, stained tissue, microbiology preparations and other specimens. Binocular heads suit routine work, while trinocular heads add a port for a camera to capture and share images. Typical objectives run from 4x to 100x oil immersion, combined with 10x eyepieces, a mechanical stage, an Abbe condenser and LED illumination. Plan achromat objectives give a flatter field across the image. Consider phase contrast or fluorescence options for specialised work, and protect optics from humidity and fungus.

products.name: Medical Tape
products.description: Medical tape secures dressings, IV cannulas, tubing and catheters to the skin. Main types include breathable paper tape for fragile skin and frequent changes, transparent plastic tape that resists water and tears easily, silk-like cloth tape with strong hold, zinc oxide tape for heavy-duty fixation and strapping, and silicone tape that removes gently. Widths of 1.25cm, 2.5cm and 5cm on 5–9 metre rolls are common. Match adhesive strength to the patient's skin condition and the device being secured, and remove tape slowly, low and close to the skin.
products.specifications: Types: paper, transparent plastic, silk-like cloth, zinc oxide, silicone; Widths: 1.25cm, 2.5cm, 5cm; Roll length: 5–9m; Adhesive: acrylic, zinc oxide or silicone; Options: hypoallergenic and latex-free
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Alcohol Swabs
products.description: Alcohol swabs are small, individually wrapped pads saturated with isopropyl alcohol, typically around 70%, used to clean skin before injections and venepuncture and to disinfect vial tops, injection ports and small equipment surfaces. Each sealed packet keeps the pad moist until opened. Allow the alcohol to dry on the skin for full effect and to reduce stinging. Alcohol swabs are not intended for open wounds, and some procedures, such as blood cultures or central line care, may call for chlorhexidine-alcohol preparations instead.
products.specifications: Solution: about 65–70% isopropyl alcohol; Pad: non-woven fabric; Packaging: individually sealed sachets; Sterility: sterile; Use: single use
products.sizes: Individually wrapped single-use swabs (~65–70% isopropyl alcohol)
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Applicators
products.description: Applicators are thin sticks tipped with absorbent cotton, used to apply ointments and antiseptics, clean small or hard-to-reach areas such as wound edges, ears, nostrils and stoma sites, and perform delicate cleaning. Wooden or plastic shafts come in single-ended and double-ended versions. Sterile individually wrapped applicators suit wound care and procedures, while non-sterile bulk packs serve general tasks. For microbiology specimens, use dedicated collection swabs, since standard cotton tips and wooden shafts can affect some laboratory tests.
products.specifications: Tip: cotton, single or double-ended; Shaft: wood or plastic; Length: standard about 15cm; Packaging: sterile individually wrapped or non-sterile bulk; Use: single use
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Tongue Depressors
products.description: Tongue depressors are flat, smooth wooden blades used to hold down the tongue during examination of the mouth and throat, and also serve as simple finger splints and spatulas for mixing or applying ointments. Adult blades are about 15cm long, with shorter, narrower paediatric versions for children. They are made from smooth, splinter-free hardwood such as birch. Non-sterile blades are common for routine examinations, while individually wrapped sterile blades suit procedures and higher-risk settings. Each blade is discarded after a single use.
products.specifications: Material: smooth hardwood, commonly birch; Adult size: about 150 x 18mm; Paediatric: shorter, narrower blade; Packaging: bulk boxes or individually wrapped; Sterility: non-sterile, sterile options
products.sizes: Adult and paediatric length wooden blades
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Nelaton Catheters
products.description: Nelaton catheters are straight, single-lumen urinary catheters with a rounded closed tip and side drainage eyes, used for short-term bladder drainage, in-and-out catheterisation and collecting sterile urine samples. Unlike Foley catheters they have no retention balloon, so they are removed once the bladder is empty. Usually made of PVC, they come in sizes from 6Fr to 20Fr with colour-coded connectors, in male, female and paediatric lengths. Choose the smallest size that drains effectively, and insert with sterile lubricant and aseptic technique.
products.specifications: Common materials include silicone, latex with coating, PVC or other polymers; sizes expressed in French/Charrière; lengths vary by patient and use; Foley designs include retention balloon; sterile single-use options common.
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Intermittent Catheters
products.description: Intermittent catheters are designed for repeated, regular bladder emptying, often by patients or caregivers performing clean intermittent self-catheterisation at home. Hydrophilic-coated versions become slippery when wetted and pre-lubricated gel versions reduce friction, while uncoated catheters need separate lubricant. Compact and ready-to-use designs, some with an integrated collection bag, make catheterisation easier away from a toilet. Sizes run from 6Fr to 20Fr, with shorter female and longer male lengths. Each catheter is sterile and single use; user dexterity and comfort guide the choice.
products.specifications: Common materials include silicone, latex with coating, PVC or other polymers; sizes expressed in French/Charrière; lengths vary by patient and use; Foley designs include retention balloon; sterile single-use options common.
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Suprapubic Catheters
products.description: Suprapubic catheters drain urine through a small opening in the lower abdomen directly into the bladder, bypassing the urethra. They are used for long-term drainage, urethral injury or obstruction, and when urethral catheters cause repeated problems. Most are silicone Foley-type catheters with a retention balloon, in sizes from 12Fr to 24Fr with various balloon capacities. Initial insertion is performed by trained clinicians, and later changes through the established tract are often done by nurses. Follow the manufacturer's guidance on maximum dwell time.
products.specifications: Common materials include silicone, latex with coating, PVC or other polymers; sizes expressed in French/Charrière; lengths vary by patient and use; Foley designs include retention balloon; sterile single-use options common.
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Urine Bags
products.description: Urine bags collect urine from an indwelling catheter in a closed drainage system. Bedside bags hold about 750mL to 2000mL and hang from the bed frame on a hanger, and are available with an outlet tap for emptying without disconnecting the system or without a tap for single fill-and-discard use. Common features include a non-return valve to prevent backflow, printed volume graduations and, on some models, a sampling port. Keep the bag below bladder level and off the floor, and empty it before it becomes full.
products.specifications: Capacity: 750–2000mL; Outlet: with or without drain tap; Valve: non-return anti-reflux; Graduations: printed volume markings; Fluid path: sterile, single use
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Leg Bags
products.description: Leg bags are body-worn urine collection bags that strap to the thigh or calf and connect to an indwelling urethral or suprapubic catheter, letting ambulant patients move around discreetly during the day. They typically hold 350 mL to 750 mL and include an inlet tube, a non-return valve to limit backflow and a lever or twist-tap outlet for emptying, with elastic straps or a fabric sleeve holding the bag in place. Choose capacity and inlet-tube length to suit the wearer's mobility and preferred bag position, and link to a larger night drainage bag for overnight use.
products.specifications: Capacity: 350–750 mL; Inlet tube: short, long or cut-to-length; Valve: non-return anti-reflux valve; Outlet: lever, push or twist tap; Fixing: elastic straps or leg sleeve; Fluid path: sterile, single use
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Urine Collection Containers
products.description: Urine collection containers are screw-cap specimen pots and larger jugs used to collect and transport urine for laboratory analysis. Sterile 60 mL and 120 mL containers are used for midstream and culture samples, non-sterile versions suit routine urinalysis, and 2–3 L containers are used for 24-hour collections for tests such as creatinine clearance or urine protein. Containers usually have a leak-resistant cap, graduated markings and a label area for patient details. Use a sterile container whenever a culture is requested, and check whether a 24-hour test requires a container with preservative added.
products.specifications: Capacity: 60 mL, 120 mL, 2–3 L (24-hour); Material: polypropylene or polystyrene; Closure: leak-resistant screw cap; Markings: graduated scale with label area; Sterility: sterile or non-sterile variants
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Urine Drainage Sets
products.description: Urine drainage sets connect to an indwelling catheter to form a closed drainage system, carrying urine through tubing into a collection bag kept below bladder level. Bedside configurations typically use a 1.5–2 L bag with a long drainage tube, bed hanger and bottom outlet tap, while leg-bag configurations suit ambulant patients. Features such as a non-return valve, needle-free sampling port and graduated volume markings support infection control and output monitoring. Keeping the system closed and the bag below the bladder helps reduce the risk of catheter-associated urinary tract infection.
products.specifications: Bag capacity: typically 1.5–2 L (bedside); Tubing: kink-resistant drainage tube; Valve: non-return anti-reflux; Sampling port: needle-free; Outlet: bottom drain tap; Accessories: bed hanger or leg straps
products.sizes: Standard bedside and leg-bag drainage configurations
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Endoscopes
products.description: Flexible endoscopes are reusable instruments with a steerable insertion tube, light guide and video or fibre-optic imaging that let clinicians examine and treat the inside of the digestive tract. Gastrointestinal types include gastroscopes for the upper tract, colonoscopes for the large bowel and side-viewing duodenoscopes for biliary and pancreatic work, in adult and paediatric diameters. A working channel passes biopsy forceps, snares and other accessories, while air/water and suction channels keep the view clear. Confirm compatibility with the facility's video processor and light source, and a validated cleaning and high-level disinfection process, before purchase.
products.specifications: Types: gastroscope, colonoscope, duodenoscope; Imaging: video or fibre-optic; Tip deflection: four-way angulation; Channels: working, air/water and suction; Sizes: adult and paediatric diameters; Reprocessing: high-level disinfection
products.precautions: Requires validated high-level disinfection/reprocessing between every patient use

products.name: Gastroscopes
products.description: Gastroscopes are forward-viewing flexible endoscopes designed for upper GI endoscopy, examining the oesophagus, stomach and duodenum. A typical adult instrument has an insertion tube of about 9 mm and a working length of around 1000 mm, with a channel of roughly 2.8 mm for biopsy forceps, injection needles and other accessories. Slim and ultra-slim versions are available for paediatric or transnasal use, while therapeutic models have larger channels for haemostasis and foreign body removal. Tip angulation, channel size and compatibility with the existing video processor are key selection points.
products.specifications: Insertion tube: approx. 9 mm (slim approx. 5–6 mm); Working length: approx. 1000–1100 mm; Working channel: approx. 2.8 mm (therapeutic 3.2 mm+); View: forward-viewing; Angulation: four-way tip deflection; Reprocessing: high-level disinfection
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Colonoscopes
products.description: Colonoscopes are long, forward-viewing flexible endoscopes used to examine the colon and terminal ileum for screening, diagnosis and therapy such as polypectomy. Adult instruments are typically about 12–13 mm in diameter with a working length of roughly 1600–1700 mm, and many offer adjustable insertion-tube stiffness to help navigate bowel loops. Paediatric colonoscopes have a smaller diameter for children or patients with a narrow or angulated colon. Working channel size matters when planning accessories, as larger channels accept bigger snares and clips and improve suction of fluid and debris.
products.specifications: Insertion tube: approx. 12–13 mm (paediatric smaller); Working length: approx. 1600–1700 mm (shorter variants exist); Working channel: approx. 3.2–3.8 mm; Stiffness: fixed or variable; View: forward-viewing, wide angle; Reprocessing: high-level disinfection
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Duodenoscopes
products.description: Duodenoscopes are side-viewing flexible endoscopes used mainly for endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP), giving a direct view of the major papilla in the duodenum. Their distinctive feature is an elevator at the tip that deflects cannulas, guidewires, sphincterotomes and stents into the bile or pancreatic duct. Typical insertion-tube diameters are around 11–12 mm, with large working channels for therapeutic accessories. Because the elevator area is complex to clean, these scopes need meticulous manual cleaning and strict adherence to reprocessing instructions; designs with disposable distal caps can simplify this.
products.specifications: View: side-viewing; Insertion tube: approx. 11–12 mm; Working channel: approx. 3.7–4.2 mm; Elevator: accessory elevator at distal tip; Working length: approx. 1240 mm; Reprocessing: high-level disinfection or sterilisation
products.precautions: Elevator-channel design is associated with higher reprocessing/cross-infection risk – follow strict reprocessing protocols

products.name: Biopsy Forceps
products.description: Endoscopic biopsy forceps are flexible instruments passed through an endoscope's working channel to take small mucosal tissue samples for histology. They consist of a coiled sheath, a pair of opening cups at the tip and a handle that opens and closes the jaws. Variants include standard and jumbo cups, fenestrated jaws, smooth or serrated edges and an optional central needle that anchors the forceps on tangential tissue. Choose shaft length to suit gastroscope or colonoscope use and match outer diameter to the scope's channel; jumbo cups need a larger therapeutic channel.
products.specifications: Cup type: standard or jumbo, oval or alligator; Jaw options: fenestrated, serrated, with or without needle; Outer diameter: approx. 1.8–2.8 mm; Working length: approx. 1600–2300 mm; Min. channel: approx. 2.0–3.2 mm
products.sizes: Standard and jumbo cup sizes, various shaft lengths
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Endoscopic Snares
products.description: Endoscopic snares are wire loops housed in a flexible plastic sheath that are passed through an endoscope channel to capture and remove polyps and other lesions. The loop is opened around the lesion and closed from the handle, cutting either cold or with electrosurgical current to cut and coagulate tissue. Loops come in hexagonal, oval and crescent shapes from about 10 mm to 30 mm, in braided or monofilament wire. Small cold snares are generally used for diminutive polyps and larger loops for bigger or pedunculated lesions; for hot snaring, confirm compatibility with the electrosurgical unit.
products.specifications: Loop shape: hexagonal, oval, crescent; Loop diameter: approx. 10–30 mm; Wire: monofilament or braided stainless steel; Working length: approx. 2300 mm; Use: cold or hot (electrosurgical)
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Endoscopic Clips
products.description: Endoscopic clips (haemoclips) are small metal clips deployed through an endoscope's working channel to control bleeding, close mucosal defects and mark lesion sites. Each clip is preloaded on a flexible applicator: the operator opens the jaws, positions them over the target, then closes and releases the clip, which typically detaches on its own days to weeks later. Many designs can be rotated and reopened before final deployment for accurate placement. Standard and long-reach applicators suit upper GI and colonic use, and jaw opening width should match the defect or vessel size.
products.specifications: Jaw opening: approx. 8–16 mm; Applicator: standard and long-reach lengths; Functions: rotatable, reopenable (design dependent); Min. channel: approx. 2.8 mm; Clip material: stainless steel or alloy
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Irrigation Tubes
products.description: Endoscopic irrigation tubes are single-use tubing sets that deliver sterile water through an endoscope's auxiliary water-jet channel or working channel to wash away blood, stool, bile or mucus and keep the visual field clear. They typically run from a water bottle or bag via an irrigation pump or flushing syringe and include a connector matched to the scope's channel port, often with a backflow-prevention valve. Sets come in different lengths and diameters for gastroscopes and colonoscopes. Confirm connector compatibility with the scope and pump in use, and replace sets as directed to limit cross-contamination.
products.specifications: Use: water-jet or working-channel irrigation; Connection: scope-specific or luer connector; Valve: one-way backflow prevention; Length: various to suit pump or bottle position; Fluid: sterile water
products.sizes: Various diameters/lengths compatible with endoscope channel
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Endoscope Cleaning Brushes
products.description: Endoscope cleaning brushes are used during manual cleaning of flexible endoscopes to remove organic debris from internal channels, valve ports and the distal tip before high-level disinfection. Channel brushes have bristles on a long flexible shaft pulled through the suction and working channels, while short or double-ended brushes clean valve cylinders and ports. Bristle diameter must match the channel: too small leaves debris behind, too large may not pass or may damage the lining. Single-use brushes avoid cleaning and inspecting brushes between uses, and sterile single-use variants are available where required.
products.specifications: Types: channel, valve-port and tip brushes; Bristle diameter: matched to channel size; Channel brush length: approx. 1500–2300 mm; Construction: nylon bristles on flexible shaft; Configuration: single- or double-ended
products.sizes: Various diameters matched to channel size
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Fetal Dopplers
products.description: Fetal Dopplers are handheld ultrasound devices that detect the fetal heartbeat and show fetal heart rate, used at antenatal visits and for intermittent auscultation in labour. A main unit with loudspeaker and digital display connects to a probe at around 2–3 MHz: 2 MHz gives deeper penetration for later pregnancy or larger patients, while 3 MHz offers good sensitivity earlier in gestation. Coupling gel is needed for signal transmission, and some units offer waterproof probes. Staff should confirm the detected rate is fetal rather than maternal by checking the mother's pulse at the same time.
products.specifications: Probe frequency: 2–3 MHz; Display: digital FHR readout with audio speaker; Form: handheld, single or interchangeable probe; Power: rechargeable or disposable batteries; Accessories: coupling gel, optional waterproof probe
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: Labour ward, antenatal clinic, gynecology clinic

products.name: Delivery Beds
products.description: Delivery beds, or birthing beds, are adjustable beds that support the mother through labour, delivery and recovery without transfer between surfaces. They usually have a retractable or removable foot section that opens access for delivery, plus leg supports or stirrups, hand grips and an adjustable backrest for different birthing positions. Electric or hydraulic models add height adjustment and Trendelenburg tilt for emergencies. Look for fluid-resistant, easy-clean upholstery, a catch basin or drainage tray, lockable castors and a mattress that can be reconfigured quickly when urgent intervention is needed.
products.specifications: Adjustment: manual, hydraulic or electric; Positions: backrest, height, Trendelenburg; Foot section: retractable or removable; Supports: leg rests or stirrups, hand grips; Mattress: fluid-resistant, sectional; Mobility: castors with brakes
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
