products.name: Infant Warmers
products.description: Infant radiant warmers are open-bed units that supply overhead radiant heat to keep newborns warm while leaving the baby fully accessible for resuscitation, assessment and procedures. A heater head above a height-adjustable bassinet tray works in manual mode or servo mode, where a skin temperature probe adjusts heat output automatically. Many units include an Apgar timer, tilting tray, X-ray cassette drawer and alarms for probe disconnection or overheating. Because the open design increases insensible water loss, radiant warmers are generally preferred for short-term care in delivery rooms and during procedures.
products.specifications: Patient age/weight range, dimensions, measurement ranges, alarms, materials and accessories vary by model; pediatric/neonatal sizing must match the manufacturer's specified patient population.
products.sizes: Open-bed radiant warmer with height-adjustable tray
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Delivery Kits
products.description: Delivery kits are sterile, single-use packs that gather the basic items needed for a normal vaginal birth, helping teams prepare quickly and maintain a clean field. A typical kit includes umbilical cord clamps, cord-cutting scissors, drapes, an under-buttocks sheet and gauze swabs, and some add gloves, a kidney dish or a mucus extractor. Contents vary between kits, so facilities should check the component list against their delivery protocol and decide whether episiotomy or suturing items are needed separately. Packs are opened at the point of care and all components discarded after one delivery.

products.sizes: Standard delivery pack (clamps, scissors, drapes, gauze)
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: Labour ward, antenatal clinic, gynecology clinic

products.name: Gynecological Examination Tables
products.description: Gynaecological examination tables are couches designed for pelvic examination, speculum and colposcopy procedures and minor gynaecological work, supporting the patient in the lithotomy position. They feature padded leg supports or stirrups, an adjustable backrest and often a drainage tray, with height adjustment that brings the patient to a comfortable working level for the clinician. Manual, hydraulic and electric versions are available. Because a disposable paper roll is commonly used over the upholstery between patients, a built-in roll holder and wipe-clean, fluid-resistant covering help with hygiene and quick turnover.
products.specifications: Adjustment: manual, hydraulic or electric; Height: adjustable working height; Leg supports: knee crutches or foot stirrups; Backrest: adjustable angle; Accessories: drainage tray, paper roll holder; Upholstery: wipe-clean, fluid-resistant
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: Labour ward, antenatal clinic, gynecology clinic

products.name: Vaginal Speculums
products.description: Vaginal speculums gently open the vaginal walls to give a clear view of the cervix for examination, cervical screening, IUD insertion and other procedures. Graves speculums have wider, curved blades suited to multiparous patients, while Pederson speculums have narrower, flatter blades for nulliparous or postmenopausal patients; both come in small, medium and large. Disposable plastic speculums are supplied sterile and some accept an attachable light source, while reusable stainless steel versions are reprocessed between patients. Choosing the smallest size that gives an adequate view improves patient comfort.
products.specifications: Types: Graves and Pederson; Sizes: small, medium, large; Material: clear plastic or stainless steel; Blade locking: ratchet or screw adjustment; Options: light source attachment (plastic types)
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: Labour ward, antenatal clinic, gynecology clinic

products.name: Colposcopes
products.description: Colposcopes are stand-mounted magnifiers used to examine the cervix, vagina and vulva in detail, typically after an abnormal cervical screening result. They provide illuminated magnification of about 6x to 40x from a working distance outside the patient, and a green filter highlights vessel patterns after acetic acid is applied. Optical models use binocular eyepieces, while video colposcopes display and record images on a monitor for documentation and teaching. Consider magnification steps, light source, fixed or mobile stand and image-capture needs, along with how the unit fits into biopsy and treatment workflows.
products.specifications: Magnification: approx. 6x–40x; Working distance: approx. 300 mm; Light source: LED or halogen; Filter: green (red-free); Mounting: fixed or mobile stand; Imaging: optical binocular or video
products.sizes: Fixed or mobile stand, 6x–40x magnification range
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: Labour ward, antenatal clinic, gynecology clinic

products.name: Gynecological Instruments
products.description: Gynaecological instruments are reusable stainless steel tools for examination and minor procedures on the cervix and uterus, such as endometrial sampling, IUD insertion and dilation and curettage. Common items include tenaculums to grasp and steady the cervix, uterine sounds to measure uterine depth, graduated cervical dilators and sharp or blunt curettes, bought individually or as procedure sets. Instruments are cleaned and sterilised between patients, so corrosion-resistant surgical-grade steel and careful tracking of set contents help maintain availability and safe reprocessing.

products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: Labour ward, antenatal clinic, gynecology clinic

products.name: Infant Incubators
products.description: Infant incubators are enclosed, transparent chambers that provide a warm, humidified and protected environment for preterm, low-birth-weight or sick newborns. Unlike open radiant warmers, they maintain a stable microclimate using servo control of air or skin temperature and adjustable humidity, which helps reduce heat and fluid loss in very small infants. Hand ports and access doors allow care with minimal disturbance, and many units offer a tilting mattress tray, integrated scale or oxygen inlet. Alarm functions, ease of cleaning between patients and whether a transport model is also needed are key considerations.
products.specifications: Patient age/weight range, dimensions, measurement ranges, alarms, materials and accessories vary by model; pediatric/neonatal sizing must match the manufacturer's specified patient population.
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Neonatal Ventilators
products.description: Neonatal ventilators provide mechanical breathing support for newborns with respiratory failure, prematurity-related lung disease or apnoea, delivering very small, precisely controlled breaths. They can deliver tidal volumes as low as about 2 mL and typically use a flow sensor at the airway to measure volumes and compensate for the endotracheal tube leaks common in infants. Modes may include pressure-controlled, volume-targeted and CPAP, and some units offer high-frequency ventilation. The ventilator is reusable while breathing circuits are typically disposable, so confirm the circuits, humidifier and sensor consumables available for the chosen model.

products.name: Phototherapy Units
products.description: Phototherapy units treat neonatal jaundice by exposing the infant's skin to blue light, which converts bilirubin into forms the body can excrete without relying on the liver to conjugate it. Overhead units sit above a cot, incubator or warmer, bili-blankets place a light-emitting pad around or under the baby, and bassinet-integrated designs build the light into the bed. Most current systems use blue LEDs. Effectiveness depends on irradiance and the skin area exposed, so units with adjustable, measurable irradiance are preferred, and eye shields are used with overhead lights.
products.specifications: Light source: blue LED (approx. 460–490 nm); Configuration: overhead, blanket/pad or bassinet; Irradiance: adjustable, standard and intensive levels; Controls: treatment timer; Accessories: eye shields, radiometer (optional)
products.precautions: Eye protection required for infant during treatment

products.name: Neonatal Monitors
products.description: Neonatal monitors are multi-parameter patient monitors configured for newborns, tracking heart rate, respiration, SpO2, temperature and non-invasive blood pressure in the NICU and nursery. They use neonatal-specific sensors, including small ECG electrodes, wrap-style oximetry probes and neonatal cuffs, with alarm limits set for newborn ranges and apnoea detection. Some support transcutaneous gas monitoring, invasive pressures or central station networking. Alongside screen visibility and alarm management, consider the ongoing supply and cost of disposable neonatal sensors, which are usually single-patient use.
products.specifications: Patient age/weight range, dimensions, measurement ranges, alarms, materials and accessories vary by model; pediatric/neonatal sizing must match the manufacturer's specified patient population.
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Pediatric Hospital Beds
products.description: Pediatric hospital beds are sized and designed for infants, children and adolescents, ranging from high-sided cots for toddlers to junior beds for older children. Full-length or high side rails help prevent falls, while adjustable height and backrest support nursing care, feeding and breathing comfort. Electric or manual models may also offer Trendelenburg positioning and a quick CPR release. Gaps between rails, mattress and frame must be small enough to prevent entrapment of small patients, and lockable castors, easy-clean surfaces and child-friendly finishes are practical points for busy paediatric wards.
products.specifications: Electric/manual adjustment depending on model; adjustable height and backrest; patient weight capacity varies; side-rail configuration; caster diameter/braking system; mattress platform dimensions; Trendelenburg/reverse Trendelenburg and CPR functions vary.
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Pediatric Pulse Oximeters
products.description: Pediatric pulse oximeters measure oxygen saturation (SpO2) and pulse rate non-invasively in infants and children by shining light through a finger, toe, hand or foot. They are used with paediatric-sized clip probes or soft wrap sensors that fit small digits and limbs, which matters because adult clips often give unreliable readings on children. Handheld and bedside units are common, often with motion-tolerant signal processing to cope with active or crying patients. Choose the probe by patient size and monitoring duration: clips suit spot checks, while wraps are better for continuous monitoring.
products.specifications: Parameters: SpO2 and pulse rate; sensor technology: optical; display type varies; adult/pediatric/neonatal sensors may be available; battery operation common; measurement range, accuracy, averaging time, alarm functions and data connectivity are model-specific.
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Pediatric Nebulizers
products.description: Pediatric nebulizers turn liquid medication into a fine mist for inhalation, delivering bronchodilators, steroids or saline to infants and children with asthma, bronchiolitis and other respiratory conditions. They are usually compressor (jet) or vibrating mesh devices supplied with child-sized face masks and mouthpieces, sometimes in playful designs that help young patients cooperate. Mesh units are quieter and more portable, while compressor models are robust and widely used on wards. A well-fitting mask is essential for children too young to use a mouthpiece, and medication cups and masks are typically disposable or single-patient items.
products.specifications: Technology: compressor/jet, vibrating mesh or ultrasonic; nebulization rate and residual volume vary; particle-size distribution varies by model; operating noise and power requirements vary; adult/pediatric masks and mouthpieces may be included.
products.sizes: Child-friendly masks, often with paediatric-sized mouthpiece
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Pediatric Scales
products.description: Pediatric scales weigh infants and children accurately so clinicians can track growth, monitor feeding and calculate weight-based medication doses. Infant scales have a curved tray that holds the baby securely and typically weigh up to about 20 kg in fine increments, while standing or seated scales are used for older children. Digital models often include tare, hold or averaging functions to give a stable reading on a moving baby. In the NICU and nursery, fine resolution and easy-clean trays are important, and some models add a length-measuring attachment for combined growth assessment.
products.specifications: Patient age/weight range, dimensions, measurement ranges, alarms, materials and accessories vary by model; pediatric/neonatal sizing must match the manufacturer's specified patient population.
products.sizes: Infant tray scales (up to ~20kg) and standing scales (older children)
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: TENS Units
products.description: TENS (transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation) units are small, battery-powered stimulators that deliver mild electrical pulses through skin electrodes to help relieve acute and chronic pain. Portable units commonly have two to four channels with adjustable intensity, pulse rate and pulse width, plus preset programmes such as conventional, burst and modulated modes. They are used in physiotherapy departments and for home pain management, with self-adhesive electrode pads replaced as their adhesion wears. Units with simple controls and clearly labelled presets suit home users, while clinicians may prefer fully adjustable parameters.
products.specifications: Channels: 2–4; Pulse rate: approx. 1–150 Hz; Pulse width: approx. 50–300 µs; Modes: conventional, burst, modulated; Power: disposable or rechargeable batteries; Electrodes: self-adhesive pads
products.precautions: Contraindicated over the heart, pregnant abdomen, or in patients with pacemakers
products.useSetting: Physiotherapy department, rehab gym, home care

products.name: Ultrasound Therapy Machines
products.description: Therapeutic ultrasound machines deliver high-frequency sound waves through a treatment head to heat and stimulate soft tissue, used in physiotherapy for musculoskeletal conditions such as tendinopathy, sprains and joint stiffness. Most have interchangeable heads at 1 MHz for deeper tissues and 3 MHz for more superficial structures, with continuous or pulsed output, adjustable intensity and a timer. Unlike diagnostic scanners, they do not produce images. Coupling gel is required and the head is kept moving during treatment; consider available head sizes and whether output can be checked periodically.
products.specifications: Frequency: 1 MHz and 3 MHz; Output mode: continuous or pulsed; Intensity: adjustable, up to approx. 2–3 W/cm²; Treatment heads: small and large, approx. 1 cm² and 5 cm²; Timer: adjustable treatment time
products.precautions: Avoid over bony prominences, eyes, malignancy, or pregnant abdomen
products.useSetting: Physiotherapy department, rehab gym, home care

products.name: Electrical Stimulation Units
products.description: Electrical stimulation units are multi-channel therapy devices used by physiotherapists for muscle strengthening and re-education, pain relief and oedema management. Going beyond basic TENS, they typically offer waveforms such as neuromuscular stimulation (NMES), interferential, Russian and high-voltage pulsed current, with programmable on/off cycles, ramp times and intensity on each channel. Clinic models may be combined with ultrasound therapy or vacuum electrodes, while portable versions support home exercise programmes. Choose according to the waveforms your service uses, the number of channels needed to treat several muscle groups at once and electrode consumable costs.
products.specifications: Channels: 2–4 or more; Waveforms: TENS, NMES, interferential, Russian, high-voltage; Controls: intensity, frequency, ramp, on/off time; Programmes: preset and user-defined; Electrodes: self-adhesive, carbon or sponge
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: Physiotherapy department, rehab gym, home care

products.name: Infrared Lamps
products.description: Infrared lamps provide superficial heat therapy by emitting infrared radiation onto the skin, used in physiotherapy to relax muscles, ease stiffness and reduce pain before exercise or manual therapy. Floor-standing models on castors and compact table-top units are available, with adjustable height and head angle to direct heat onto the treatment area. A protective guard over the bulb and a treatment timer support safe use. Lamps should be set at the recommended distance from the skin, and clinicians should check skin sensation beforehand and monitor the patient during treatment to avoid burns.
products.specifications: Type: floor-standing or table-top; Adjustment: height and head angle; Heat source: infrared bulb or emitter; Controls: on/off with treatment timer; Safety: protective guard; Power: mains
products.precautions: Burn risk with prolonged/close exposure – maintain safe distance and treatment time
products.useSetting: Physiotherapy department, rehab gym, home care

products.name: Heat Therapy Units
products.description: Heat therapy units, such as hydrocollators, are thermostatically controlled water tanks that keep hot packs at treatment temperature, ready for moist heat therapy in physiotherapy. Packs filled with silica gel or bentonite absorb heat and are wrapped in towelling covers before being placed on the neck, back, shoulders or limbs to relieve muscle spasm and stiffness. Tanks come in sizes holding a few to many packs, with standard, neck and oversize pack shapes. Choose tank capacity by patient throughput, and use enough insulating layers between pack and skin to prevent burns.
products.specifications: Unit: stainless steel heated water tank; Temperature: thermostatic, approx. 70–75°C; Capacity: from a few to a dozen or more packs; Packs: silica gel or bentonite, various shapes; Accessories: towelling pack covers
products.sizes: Hydrocollator units and hot pack sets, various sizes
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: Physiotherapy department, rehab gym, home care

products.name: Walking Frames
products.description: Walking frames are lightweight four-legged mobility aids that give users a wide, stable base of support, used in rehabilitation after surgery, falls or illness and for long-term mobility. Standard frames are lifted and moved forward with each step, while front-wheeled frames are pushed for a smoother gait, and folding models aid transport and storage. Height-adjustable legs allow fitting, and bariatric frames offer higher weight capacity. The handgrips are usually set at wrist height with the user standing upright, and rubber ferrules should be checked regularly for wear.
products.specifications: Frame: aluminium or steel; Types: standard, front-wheeled, folding, bariatric; Height: adjustable push-button legs; Weight capacity: standard and bariatric ratings; Tips: rubber ferrules or front castors
products.sizes: Adjustable height, standard and bariatric weight capacity
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: Physiotherapy department, rehab gym, home care

products.name: Crutches
products.description: Crutches transfer part of the body's weight from the legs to the arms, allowing patients to walk with reduced or no weight-bearing through an injured leg. Axillary (underarm) crutches give more support and are often used short-term after injury or surgery, while forearm (elbow) crutches with cuffs suit longer-term users but need more upper-body strength and coordination. Both are height-adjustable and come in paediatric to adult sizes. Correct fitting matters: axillary crutch tops should sit a few finger-widths below the armpit to avoid nerve pressure, and handgrips should allow a slight elbow bend.
products.specifications: Types: axillary and forearm/elbow; Frame: aluminium; Adjustment: push-button height adjustment; Sizes: paediatric, adult, tall; Tips: non-slip rubber ferrules; Padding: underarm pads and handgrips
products.sizes: Adjustable height; axillary and forearm/elbow variants; paediatric to adult
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: Physiotherapy department, rehab gym, home care

products.name: Canes
products.description: Walking canes are single-handed mobility aids that improve balance and offload some weight from a weaker leg, for people who need less support than crutches or a walking frame. Single-point canes are light and suit mild balance problems, while tripod and quad canes have a broader base that stands on its own and gives more stability, often used after a stroke. Most are height-adjustable aluminium with offset or crook handles. A cane is usually held in the hand opposite the affected leg with the handle at about wrist height, and worn rubber tips should be replaced.
products.specifications: Types: single-point, tripod, quad base; Material: aluminium (adjustable); Height: push-button adjustment; Handle: crook, offset or ergonomic grip; Tip: non-slip rubber ferrule; Quad base: small or large
products.sizes: Adjustable height; single-point, tripod, quad-point variants
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: Physiotherapy department, rehab gym, home care

products.name: Parallel Bars
products.description: Parallel bars are a pair of fixed handrails used in physiotherapy for gait training, standing balance and early mobilisation, letting patients practise walking with secure handholds on both sides. Rails are height-adjustable and often width-adjustable to fit children and adults, mounted on a stable floor-standing base or platform. Some models include an abduction board, a mirror at the end of the walkway or a non-slip platform. Choose a length that suits the available space and training goals, and check adjustment locks and base stability regularly, since patients may bear considerable weight through the rails.
products.specifications: Length: approx. 2–4 m; Height: adjustable, child to adult; Width: adjustable between rails; Rails: wood or steel; Base: floor-standing platform or fixed uprights; Options: abduction board, gait mirror
products.sizes: Adjustable height and width, fixed floor-standing
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: Physiotherapy department, rehab gym, home care

products.name: Exercise Bikes
products.description: Rehabilitation exercise bikes are stationary cycles used to build cardiovascular fitness, lower-limb strength and joint range of motion in physiotherapy, cardiac and post-operative rehabilitation. Recumbent and seated designs with a backrest and step-through frame are easier and safer to mount for older or deconditioned patients than upright bikes. Resistance is adjustable, often magnetically, and displays show time, speed, distance and sometimes heart rate, while some models start at very low resistance or add arm cranks for upper-body work. Check seat adjustment range, maximum user weight and footprint for the space available.
products.specifications: Type: recumbent or seated upright; Resistance: magnetic or friction, adjustable levels; Display: time, speed, distance, heart rate; Access: step-through frame; Seat: adjustable position with backrest
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: Physiotherapy department, rehab gym, home care

products.name: Rehabilitation Steps
products.description: Rehabilitation steps are training stairs used in physiotherapy to practise stair climbing before discharge, after joint replacement, stroke, injury or prolonged illness. Units range from single or double step blocks to straight or corner staircases with handrails on both sides, and some allow step height to be adjusted as the patient progresses. Non-slip treads and a rigid, stable frame are essential for safety. Choose a design whose step height and handrail layout reflect the stairs the patient will face at home, and consider whether a top platform is needed for turning.
products.specifications: Configuration: single step, double step or staircase; Step height: adjustable or fixed; Treads: non-slip surface; Handrails: one or both sides (staircase models); Frame: wood or steel
products.sizes: Adjustable step height, single or double-step units
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: Physiotherapy department, rehab gym, home care

products.name: Ultrasound Machines
products.description: Cart-based ultrasound machines are full-size diagnostic scanners used in radiology and imaging departments for abdominal, obstetric, vascular, cardiac, musculoskeletal and small-parts examinations. A processing unit, large monitor and control panel sit on a wheeled cart with several transducer ports, so linear, convex, phased-array and endocavity probes can stay connected. Imaging modes typically include B-mode, M-mode and colour and spectral Doppler, with advanced software options on some systems. Match the probe set and software packages to the department's examination mix, and confirm image storage and PACS connectivity.
products.specifications: Imaging modes may include B-mode, M-mode and color/spectral Doppler; transducer types include linear, convex and phased-array; probe frequency and bandwidth vary; display size, storage, DICOM/network connectivity and battery options vary.
products.sterility: Non-sterile (sterile probe cover for invasive use)
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Portable Ultrasound Systems
products.description: Portable ultrasound systems are compact, battery-powered scanners in laptop-style or handheld formats, used for point-of-care imaging at the bedside and in emergency and outreach settings as well as imaging departments. They provide core B-mode and often colour Doppler imaging with one or a few interchangeable probes, and handheld types may use a tablet or smartphone as the display. Compared with cart-based systems they trade some image quality and features for mobility and fast start-up. Battery life, probe options, durability and how images are transferred to the patient record are key considerations.
products.specifications: Imaging modes may include B-mode, M-mode and color/spectral Doppler; transducer types include linear, convex and phased-array; probe frequency and bandwidth vary; display size, storage, DICOM/network connectivity and battery options vary.
products.sterility: Non-sterile (sterile probe cover for invasive use)
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Ultrasound Probes
products.description: Ultrasound probes (transducers) convert electrical signals into sound waves and back, and the probe type largely determines what a system can image. Linear probes use higher frequencies for superficial structures such as vessels, thyroid and musculoskeletal tissue; convex probes use lower frequencies for abdominal and obstetric scans; phased-array probes have a small footprint for cardiac imaging between the ribs; and endocavity probes are used for transvaginal and transrectal examinations. Probes must be compatible with the specific ultrasound system, and invasive use requires a sterile cover and appropriate disinfection between patients.
products.specifications: Types: linear, convex, phased-array, endocavity; Linear frequency: approx. 5–15 MHz; Convex frequency: approx. 2–6 MHz; Phased-array frequency: approx. 1–5 MHz; Endocavity frequency: approx. 4–10 MHz; Compatibility: system-specific connector
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Ultrasound Printers
products.description: Ultrasound printers are compact thermal video printers that produce instant hard-copy images from ultrasound scanners, commonly used for obstetric pictures, report attachments and patient files. They connect to the scanner by video or USB output and print in black-and-white on thermal paper, with some colour models using dedicated media. Most are small enough to mount on the ultrasound cart. Selection depends on the scanner's output connections, required print size and paper type, and the running cost of thermal paper, especially where departments rely mainly on digital storage and print only on request.
products.specifications: Print type: thermal, monochrome (colour variants available); Paper: thermal roll, commonly 110 mm wide; Connection: analogue video and/or USB; Media: standard or high-density/glossy thermal paper; Mounting: on-cart or desktop
products.sizes: Standard thermal printer, various paper widths
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Digital X-Ray Systems
products.description: Digital X-ray systems are fixed, room-based radiography installations that capture images on a digital flat-panel detector instead of film, displaying them within seconds for review. A typical room includes a high-frequency generator, an X-ray tube on a ceiling or floor mount, a patient table and a wall stand for chest and upright studies. Digital capture removes chemical processing, allows image adjustment after exposure and supports sending images to PACS. Planning considerations include room shielding, power supply, detector size and whether one or two detectors are needed for table and wall-stand workflow.
products.specifications: Generator power, kVp/mA range, exposure control, detector type, image size, mobility and digital connectivity vary; portable systems specify battery/runtime or power requirements; radiation protection and regulatory requirements apply.
products.sizes: Fixed room-based systems with digital detector panel
products.precautions: Requires radiation shielding room, licensed operator, and dosimetry monitoring

products.name: Portable X-Ray Machines
products.description: Portable X-ray machines are lightweight, compact units that can be carried or wheeled to the patient when moving them to radiology is impractical, such as on wards, in ICU and emergency departments and at outreach sites. Smaller than trolley-based mobile systems, they run on battery or mains power and are typically paired with a wireless digital detector or computed radiography cassettes. Their lower output compared with fixed rooms suits chest and extremity imaging. Operators must maintain radiation safety around nearby patients and staff, so consider exposure range, battery capacity, weight and stand options.
products.specifications: Generator power, kVp/mA range, exposure control, detector type, image size, mobility and digital connectivity vary; portable systems specify battery/runtime or power requirements; radiation protection and regulatory requirements apply.
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: Ward, ICU, emergency department, remote/outreach sites

products.name: Mobile X-Ray Systems
products.description: Mobile X-ray systems are trolley-mounted radiography units pushed or motor-driven to the bedside for patients who cannot be moved, commonly used for chest and bedside films in wards, ICU, theatres and emergency departments. They carry a generator, articulating tube arm and often an integrated digital detector and display, so images can be reviewed at the bedside. Motor-assisted drive and a compact footprint make it easier to manoeuvre between beds. Consider generator power, battery capacity for full rounds, detector integration and tube-arm reach when choosing a system.
products.specifications: Generator power, kVp/mA range, exposure control, detector type, image size, mobility and digital connectivity vary; portable systems specify battery/runtime or power requirements; radiation protection and regulatory requirements apply.
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: X-Ray Accessories
products.description: X-ray accessories are the supporting items that make radiography safe and effective, including anti-scatter grids, cassettes, lead aprons and thyroid shields, and positioning or anatomical markers. Grids improve image contrast by absorbing scattered radiation, cassettes hold film or imaging plates, and lead-equivalent garments shield staff and patients from unnecessary exposure, while left and right markers identify orientation on the image. Choose cassette and grid sizes to match the equipment in use, select apron lead equivalence and fit according to the tasks performed, and inspect protective garments periodically for cracks.
products.specifications: Generator power, kVp/mA range, exposure control, detector type, image size, mobility and digital connectivity vary; portable systems specify battery/runtime or power requirements; radiation protection and regulatory requirements apply.
products.sizes: Grids, cassettes, lead aprons/markers, various sizes
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: C-Arms
products.description: C-arms are mobile fluoroscopy systems with an X-ray source and image receptor mounted at opposite ends of a C-shaped arm, providing real-time imaging during surgery and interventional procedures. They are widely used in orthopaedic and trauma theatres, pain management, urology and vascular work, where the arm rotates around the patient without moving them. Systems use either an image intensifier or a flat-panel detector, with a separate monitor cart for live and stored images. The arm is covered with sterile drapes in theatre; consider detector size, rotation range, dose-reduction features and manoeuvring space.
products.specifications: Detector: image intensifier (approx. 9–12 in) or flat panel; Imaging: continuous and pulsed fluoroscopy, spot images; Movement: orbital and angular rotation; Display: monitor cart with image storage; Drapes: sterile covers for OR use
products.sizes: Mobile fluoroscopy unit, various image-intensifier/flat-panel sizes
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.
products.useSetting: Operating room, cath lab, orthopaedic theatre

products.name: Mammography Systems
products.description: Mammography systems are dedicated X-ray units that image breast tissue at low dose for breast cancer screening and diagnostic assessment. A compression paddle flattens and holds the breast against a digital detector to reduce motion and tissue overlap, while a low-kilovoltage tube with molybdenum, rhodium or tungsten target optimises soft-tissue contrast. Many digital systems also offer tomosynthesis (3D imaging) and support stereotactic biopsy. Planning should cover room shielding, review workstation requirements, an ongoing quality control programme and whether screening volumes justify tomosynthesis capability.
products.specifications: Detector: digital flat panel, approx. 24 × 30 cm; Tube voltage: low kVp, typically approx. 25–35; Anode: molybdenum, rhodium or tungsten; Compression: motorised with manual release; Options: tomosynthesis, stereotactic biopsy
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: CT Scanners
products.description: A computed tomography scanner acquires multiple X-ray projections around the patient and reconstructs cross-sectional images. CT systems are specified according to detector configuration, gantry design, patient table, image quality, dose management, reconstruction software and clinical applications.
products.specifications: Detector configuration, slice/reconstruction capabilities, gantry aperture, scan range, tube rating, table load capacity, spatial/contrast resolution, dose-management tools and DICOM connectivity vary by model.
products.sizes: Bore diameter typically 70–80cm; slice count varies by model
products.precautions: Requires dedicated shielded suite, licensed radiographer, and radiation dose monitoring

products.name: MRI Systems
products.description: An MRI system produces detailed images using a strong magnetic field and radiofrequency energy without ionizing radiation. Systems are selected according to field strength, clinical applications, gradient performance, bore size, patient table capacity, coils, siting requirements and infrastructure.
products.specifications: Field strength commonly 1.5T or 3T in many clinical systems; bore diameter, gradient performance, slew rate, RF coils, table capacity, cooling/infrastructure and software packages vary; MRI safety controls are essential.
products.precautions: Strict ferromagnetic-object exclusion zone; screen all patients/staff/equipment before entry

products.name: Medical Refrigerators
products.description: Medical refrigerators are purpose-built cold storage units that hold temperature-sensitive medicines, reagents and laboratory samples within a tight 2–8°C range, avoiding the fluctuations of domestic fridges. They use forced-air circulation for even temperature, a digital controller and display, and audible and visual alarms for high or low temperature and door-open events. Capacities typically run from about 100 L to 700 L in under-counter and upright formats, with solid or glass doors and lockable access. Data logging or remote monitoring helps document temperature control, and siting away from heat sources supports stable performance.
products.specifications: Temperature range depends on application; net capacity, temperature uniformity, recovery time, digital monitoring, alarms, door configuration and backup power options vary by model.
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Pharmacy Refrigerators
products.description: Pharmacy refrigerators store refrigerated medicines such as insulin, some antibiotics, eye drops and biologics at 2–8°C in hospital pharmacies and ward medication rooms. They are designed around dispensing workflow, with adjustable shelves or drawers for stock rotation and segregation, glass doors so stock can be checked without opening, and locks to restrict access. Fan-assisted cooling, minimum/maximum temperature display and alarms help keep contents in range. Capacities usually span about 100 L to 600 L; choose a size that avoids overfilling, since tightly packed shelves block airflow and create warm spots.
products.specifications: Temperature range depends on application; net capacity, temperature uniformity, recovery time, digital monitoring, alarms, door configuration and backup power options vary by model.
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Vaccine Refrigerators
products.description: Vaccine refrigerators keep vaccines within the 2–8°C range needed to preserve potency, with tighter temperature stability and protection than general-purpose units. Types include mains-powered upright or chest units, ice-lined models that hold temperature through power cuts, and solar direct-drive units for sites with unreliable electricity, which suits immunisation clinics and remote facilities. Typical capacities are about 100 L to 300 L. Continuous temperature monitoring with a data logger, freeze protection and an organised storage layout help prevent freezing, which can irreversibly damage many vaccines.
products.specifications: Temperature range depends on application; net capacity, temperature uniformity, recovery time, digital monitoring, alarms, door configuration and backup power options vary by model.
products.precautions: Continuous temperature logging required per national/WHO cold-chain guidance

products.name: Medication Cabinets
products.description: Medication cabinets are lockable cupboards that keep medicines in pharmacies, ward medication rooms and clinics organised, secure and away from unauthorised access. They are usually powder-coated or stainless steel with adjustable shelves, bins or drawers, in wall-mounted and floor-standing formats, including double-locked cabinets for controlled drugs and glass-fronted designs for visibility. Clear labelling and bin dividers support stock rotation and reduce picking errors. Select the lock type and security level according to the class of medicines stored and local controlled-drug storage rules.
products.specifications: Material: powder-coated or stainless steel; Mounting: wall-mounted or floor-standing; Interior: adjustable shelves, bins or drawers; Locking: key, combination or electronic; Options: double-lock controlled-drug compartment, glass doors
products.precautions: Controlled-drug variants require compliant locking per local pharmacy regulation

products.name: Automated Dispensing Cabinets
products.description: Automated dispensing cabinets are computer-controlled medication storage units on wards or in pharmacies that release medicines only to authorised users and record every transaction. Staff log in by password, card or fingerprint, select a patient and medicine, and the cabinet unlocks only the drawer, pocket or lidded compartment holding it. This supports controlled-drug security, real-time stock tracking, restocking reports and fewer selection errors, with drawer layouts ranging from open matrix drawers to single-dose locked pockets. Integration with pharmacy and ordering systems is a key consideration, along with network, backup power and staff training.
products.specifications: Storage: matrix drawers, lidded pockets, locked towers; Access: password, ID card or biometric; Software: transaction logging and inventory reports; Integration: pharmacy and ordering system interface; Options: refrigerated compartment, auxiliary cabinets
products.precautions: Requires reliable power/network connectivity and periodic stock reconciliation

products.name: Tablet Counters
products.description: Tablet counters help pharmacy staff count tablets and capsules accurately and hygienically when dispensing. Manual counting trays have a raised counting area, a spatula and a channel or spout that returns excess tablets to the stock bottle, while electronic counters use optical sensors or weighing to count units as they are poured or fed through. Electronic models speed up high-volume dispensing and reduce miscounts. Counting surfaces should be cleaned between medicines to prevent cross-contamination, and dedicated trays are often kept for cytotoxic drugs or allergens such as penicillins.
products.specifications: Types: manual tray or electronic counter; Manual design: tray with spatula and return spout; Electronic counting: optical sensor or weight-based; Material: plastic or stainless steel; Cleaning: wipe-clean counting surfaces
products.sizes: Manual tray or electronic counting units
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Pill Crushers
products.description: Pill crushers are handheld devices that grind tablets into powder so they can be mixed with soft food or liquid, or given through a feeding tube, for patients who cannot swallow tablets whole. Common designs use a screw-down, twist or lever action to crush tablets in a cup, and many work with disposable pouches or cups that contain the powder and reduce cross-contamination between patients; some also split tablets. Not every tablet is suitable for crushing, particularly modified-release, enteric-coated and some hazardous medicines, so pharmacy guidance should be checked first.
products.specifications: Mechanism: screw-down, twist or lever; Operation: manual, handheld; Consumables: disposable crushing pouches or cups; Body: plastic or metal; Options: combined crusher and splitter
products.precautions: Never crush enteric-coated/extended-release tablets unless confirmed safe to do so

products.name: Medication Trolleys
products.description: Medication trolleys are mobile, lockable carts used to carry and give medicines during ward rounds, keeping patients' medicines organised and secure at the bedside. They usually have multiple drawers or cassette bins, a work surface and key, code or electronic locking, with optional controlled-drug compartments, waste bins and holders for charts or a computer. Some designs use individual patient drawers for unit-dose systems. Choose a drawer layout that matches the ward's dispensing system, and check castor quality, manoeuvrability and how quickly the trolley can be locked when left unattended.
products.specifications: Body: steel, aluminium or ABS plastic; Drawers: multi-drawer or patient-specific cassettes; Locking: key, combination or electronic; Castors: swivel with brakes; Options: controlled-drug box, side bins, laptop shelf
products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: IV Preparation Equipment
products.description: IV preparation equipment provides a controlled clean environment for aseptic compounding of intravenous medicines, parenteral nutrition and cytotoxic drugs in hospital pharmacies. Main types are laminar airflow cabinets, which pass HEPA-filtered air over the work area, biological safety cabinets that also protect the operator when handling hazardous drugs, and enclosed isolators with glove ports. Sterile disposable consumables such as syringes and transfer sets are used inside the controlled zone. Aseptic technique remains essential, so choose equipment according to the drugs prepared, the room classification and cleaning and validation requirements.
products.specifications: Types: laminar airflow cabinet, biological safety cabinet, isolator; Filtration: HEPA-filtered air; Airflow: horizontal or vertical unidirectional; Work surface: stainless steel; Monitoring: airflow alarm or indicator
products.sizes: Laminar airflow cabinets/isolators, various chamber sizes
products.precautions: Aseptic technique and correct airflow/certification required for sterile compounding

products.name: Dental Chairs
products.description: Dental chairs are electrically adjustable patient chairs that position patients for examination and treatment so the dentist and assistant can reach the mouth comfortably. Motors control seat height, backrest recline and headrest position, often with programmable memory positions and a foot control so the clinician can adjust the chair without using their hands. Upholstery is typically seamless and wipe-clean, with disposable barrier covers on high-touch areas between patients. When buying a chair on its own, check compatibility with existing delivery units, lights and suction, along with patient weight capacity and footprint.
products.specifications: Materials commonly include stainless steel, polymers or coated components; dimensions, adjustment ranges, operating speeds, power requirements and accessories vary by product.

products.name: Dental Units
products.description: Dental units are integrated treatment centres combining a patient chair, instrument delivery unit, operating light, assistant's module and often a cuspidor in one system. The delivery unit holds handpiece hoses, an air/water syringe and sometimes an ultrasonic scaler or curing light, while the assistant's side carries high- and low-volume suction. Delivery can be mounted over the patient, at the side or behind the chair, which affects four-handed working. Key selection factors include waterline disinfection, the number of instrument positions, compatibility with existing compressors and suction plant, and team ergonomics.

products.name: Dental X-Ray Machines
products.description: Dental X-ray machines are small radiography units used to take intraoral images such as bitewing and periapical views for diagnosing caries, periodontal bone loss and root problems. Wall-mounted units use an articulating arm to position the tube head at the patient's mouth, while handheld or portable units allow imaging in small clinics and outreach settings. They are used with digital sensors, phosphor plates or film. Rectangular collimation and fast image receptors help reduce patient dose, and installation must account for operator distance and shielding requirements.

products.precautions: Requires radiation shielding/positioning and licensed operator

products.name: Dental Autoclaves
products.description: Dental autoclaves are benchtop steam sterilisers used to sterilise handpieces, instruments and other reusable items in dental clinics. Chamber capacities are usually about 8 L to 23 L, and cycles typically run at around 121°C or 134°C depending on the load. Pre-vacuum models remove air from hollow and wrapped loads such as handpieces and pouched instruments, while simpler gravity cycles suit only unwrapped solid instruments. Cycle printing or data logging, a drying phase and water quality are practical considerations, and routine tests are needed to confirm the steriliser is performing correctly.

products.name: Dental Suction Systems
products.description: Dental suction systems remove saliva, water, blood and aerosols from the mouth during treatment, keeping the field clear and reducing airborne contamination. A central vacuum unit connects to high-volume evacuator tubes and low-volume saliva ejectors at each chair, with disposable tips changed between patients. In dry systems fluid is separated near the chair, while wet systems carry fluid and air together to the vacuum unit. Size the system for the number of chairs used at the same time, and plan for amalgam separation where required and regular cleaning of suction lines.

products.name: Dental Mirrors
products.description: Dental mirrors are handheld instruments with a small round mirror head used to view hard-to-see tooth surfaces, reflect light into the mouth and retract the cheek or tongue during examination and treatment. Common head sizes are No. 4 and No. 5, about 22 mm and 24 mm, on screw-in or cone-socket fittings that attach to compatible handles. Front-surface mirrors give a sharper single image than rear-surface designs. Heads are cleaned and sterilised between patients and replaced when scratched or cloudy, since a worn surface reduces visibility.

products.precautions: Follow manufacturer instructions for use, storage and reprocessing (where applicable); verify compatibility with facility protocols before use.

products.name: Dental Probes
products.description: Dental probes are fine-tipped instruments used to examine teeth and gums. Periodontal probes have a blunt, millimetre-marked tip for measuring pocket depth and attachment loss during periodontal charting, while explorers have a sharp point for detecting calculus, restoration margins and surface irregularities. Designs include colour-banded and ball-ended periodontal probes and double-ended explorer and probe combinations. Stainless steel probes are reprocessed and sterilised between patients, disposable plastic versions are available for single use, and markings must stay clearly legible for accurate charting.

products.name: Dental Forceps
products.description: Dental forceps are hinged extraction instruments with beaks shaped to grip specific teeth, used to luxate and remove teeth in dental clinics and oral surgery. Upper forceps have straight or bayonet-style handles aligned with the maxillary arch, while lower forceps have beaks set roughly at right angles to the handles for the mandible. Patterns are tooth-specific, for example incisors and canines, premolars, molars with beaks that engage the root furcation, and root fragments. Clinics typically stock sets covering adult and child teeth, and hinge action and beak alignment should be checked regularly.

products.name: Dental Scalers
products.description: Dental scalers remove calculus, plaque and stains from tooth surfaces during routine cleaning and periodontal treatment. Hand scalers, such as sickle scalers for deposits above the gumline, have sharp working edges that need regular sharpening, while related curettes have rounded tips for work below the gumline. Ultrasonic and other powered scalers vibrate a fine tip at high frequency with a water spray to break up deposits and flush the area. Powered units need compatible tips or inserts and a water supply, and high-volume suction is recommended to control aerosols.

products.name: Dental Extraction Instruments
products.description: Dental extraction instruments are the hand instruments used to loosen and remove teeth, combining elevators and luxators with extraction forceps. Straight, Cryer and other elevators are wedged between tooth and bone to stretch ligament fibres and lift the tooth or root, while luxators have thinner, sharper blades for gentler, bone-preserving work; forceps then grasp and deliver the tooth. Instruments come in tooth-specific and left/right paired patterns. Clinics usually assemble procedure trays for common extraction types, and blade tips should be inspected for damage after each reprocessing cycle.

products.description: Sharps containers are rigid, puncture-resistant, single-use boxes for disposing of used needles, scalpel blades, lancets and other sharps at the point of use. Typical sizes range from 0.5 L for trays and phlebotomy carts to 10 L for treatment rooms, with a restricted opening, needle-removal notches and a temporary closure for when the container is not in use. Once filled to the marked fill line, the lid is locked permanently for disposal. Choose sizes that can sit within arm's reach of where sharps are used, and mount or position containers so they stay upright and stable.

products.name: Biohazard Waste Bins
products.description: Biohazard waste bins are lidded collection bins for infectious clinical waste such as contaminated dressings, gloves and disposable items, lined with colour-coded disposable bags. Common capacities range from about 20 L to 120 L, and foot-pedal or sensor lids allow hands-free opening to reduce contamination. Bins are typically made of durable, wipe-clean plastic or steel and display the biohazard symbol. The bin itself is reusable and should be cleaned regularly, while liners are tied off and removed before overfilling. Place bins where infectious waste is generated and match colours to the local segregation scheme.

products.name: Clinical Waste Bags
products.description: Clinical waste bags are colour-coded disposable liners that contain infectious and other healthcare waste for collection, storage and treatment. Yellow is commonly used for infectious waste, with other colours assigned under local segregation rules, and bags often carry the biohazard symbol. Typical capacities of 20 L, 50 L, 80 L and 120 L fit standard bins and trolleys. Bag thickness and tear resistance matter for heavy or wet loads; bags should be filled to no more than about three-quarters, securely tied or sealed, and labelled with their source for traceability.

products.name: Pharmaceutical Waste Containers

Sizes range from about 1 L for medication rooms to 20 L for pharmacies, usually with a secure closure that locks once full. Separate containers with distinct colour coding are often used for cytotoxic or other hazardous drugs. Correct segregation matters because pharmaceutical waste usually needs incineration or other specific treatment, so containers should be clearly labelled with the waste category.

They are usually made of rigid plastic or metal with closed bodies and lids that contain bags and prevent spills, and lockable lids restrict access during transport and storage. Sizes range from small ward carts to large wheeled bins. Smooth, wipe-clean surfaces and drain points help with disinfection, and dedicated trolleys colour-coded for each waste stream keep waste separated all the way to disposal.

Each bin is labelled with its colour, symbol and accepted items, and sets may be freestanding, held in a shared frame or mounted on a trolley. Capacities can be mixed to match how much of each waste type an area generates. Segregating at source reduces the volume of waste needing costly treatment, and the colour scheme should follow local waste management rules.

products.name: Needle Destroyers
products.description: Needle destroyers render used hypodermic needles unusable immediately after an injection, reducing needlestick injuries and preventing reuse. Electric benchtop units melt or burn the needle using an electric arc or resistive heating, while manual or mechanical units cut the needle from the syringe hub into a sealed collection container, with residues then disposed of as sharps waste. Consider which needle sizes the unit accepts, power or battery availability and the residue container capacity. Units are most useful at the point of use, such as injection rooms and vaccination stations.

Autoclave-based systems use pressurised steam, often combined with shredding to reduce volume and make waste unrecognisable, while chemical systems combine disinfectants with mechanical maceration. Throughput ranges from compact units for a single facility to larger systems serving several sites. Selection depends on daily waste volume and type, space and utilities, operator training and the validation testing needed to show effective treatment; pharmaceutical and some chemical waste need other disposal routes.

products.description: Home oxygen concentrators draw in room air and use molecular sieve beds to remove nitrogen, delivering concentrated oxygen through a nasal cannula or mask for long-term oxygen therapy at home. Stationary units run on mains power and commonly provide continuous flow up to about 5 L/min, while portable battery models often use pulse-dose delivery to save oxygen when the patient is mobile. Concentrators reduce reliance on frequent cylinder deliveries. Patients should use the prescribed flow rate, keep the unit ventilated and away from open flames, and have a backup cylinder in case of power failure.

Kits usually include a medication cup, tubing, mouthpiece and adult or child masks, which are replaced periodically. The medication cup should be cleaned and dried after each use, and the device should suit the prescribed medication.
